Contains documents and further evidence from the case |url=http://www.ct.gov/csao/lib/csao/compressed-sandy-hook-report.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131125213507/http://www.ct.gov/csao/lib/csao/compressed-sandy-hook-report.pdf |archive-date=November 25, 2013 |access-date=December 7, 2013}}</ref> Lanza's body was found wearing a pale green pocket vest over a black polo shirt over a black T-shirt, along with black sneakers, black fingerless gloves, black socks, and a black canvas belt.<ref name="ct.gov" /> Other objects found in the vicinity of Lanza included a black [[boonie hat]] and thin frame sunglasses. The Glock was found, apparently jammed, near Lanza, and the rifle was found several feet away from him.<ref name="ct.gov" /> A [[9×19mm Parabellum|9mm]] [[SIG Sauer P226]], which had not been fired during the incident, was also found on Lanza.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Marcus |first=Ruth |date=May 17, 2023 |title=Opinion {{!}} Nancy Lanza, a mother tragic and infuriating |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/ruth-marcus-nancy-lanza-a-mother-tragic-and-infuriating/2013/11/26/30efee1c-56cb-11e3-835d-e7173847c7cc_story.html |access-date=October 13, 2024 |newspaper=Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286 |archive-date=February 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220216200215/https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/ruth-marcus-nancy-lanza-a-mother-tragic-and-infuriating/2013/11/26/30efee1c-56cb-11e3-835d-e7173847c7cc_story.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Lanza shot all but two of his victims multiple times. Most of the shooting took place in two first-grade classrooms near the entrance of the school. The students among the victims totaled eight boys and twelve girls, all either six or seven years old, and the six adults were all women who worked at the school. Eighteen children were pronounced dead at the school and two were pronounced dead at [[Danbury Hospital]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Susman |first1=Tina |last2=Quinones |first2=Sam |title=Bodies of shooting victims are removed from elementary school |url=https://www.latimes.com/nation/la-xpm-2012-dec-15-la-na-nn-sandy-hook-school-shooting-bodies-20121215-story.html |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 10, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241111151759/https://www.latimes.com/nation/la-xpm-2012-dec-15-la-na-nn-sandy-hook-school-shooting-bodies-20121215-story.html |archive-date=November 11, 2024 |date=December 15, 2012}}</ref> As of the present day, the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting is the [[List of school shootings in the United States by death toll#List|second deadliest school shooting in U.S. history]].<ref name="winter-2022">{{Cite magazine |last=Winter |first=Jessica |date=2022-05-25 |title=Seeing America, Again, in the Uvalde Elementary-School Shooting |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/daily-comment/seeing-america-again-in-the-texas-elementary-school-shooting |access-date=2025-08-20 |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X |archive-date=May 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220527194747/https://www.newyorker.com/news/daily-comment/seeing-america-again-in-the-texas-elementary-school-shooting |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Possible motives for shooting ===
While official investigations concluded that Lanza's motive may never be known, they identified several events and psychological factors that likely contributed to his decision.<ref name="Thomas & Rabe">{{Cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Arielle Levin Becker |last2=Rabe |first2=Jacqueline |date=2014-11-21 |title=Newtown shooter: Report finds failure to address 'a cascade' of problems |url=https://ctmirror.org/2014/11/21/four-things-to-learn-from-the-life-of-newtown-shooter-adam-lanza/ |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=CT Mirror |language=en-US |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201172240/https://ctmirror.org/2014/11/21/four-things-to-learn-from-the-life-of-newtown-shooter-adam-lanza/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=The Enigma of Adam Lanza's Mind and Motivations for Murder |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/294091435 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001110203/https://www.researchgate.net/publication/294091435_The_Enigma_of_Adam_Lanza%27s_Mind_and_Motivations_for_Murder |archive-date=October 1, 2023 |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=ResearchGate |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> In messages to a fellow gamer, he wrote, "I incessantly have nothing other than scorn for humanity".<ref name="courant-2018-docs"/><ref name="nypost-2018"/>
Counseling psychologist [[Peter F. Langman]] has suggested that Lanza suffered from [[narcissism]] and [[solipsism]], a state where he perceived other people as "cardboard cut-outs" without real value, which removed any moral constraint against killing them.<ref name="langman-2015"/> However, the FBI found no evidence that Lanza believed his attack to be a video game or game.<ref name="providence-journal-2017"/>

While Lanza had [[Asperger's syndrome]], [[obsessive–compulsive disorder]] (OCD), and severe anxiety, commentators emphasize these did not cause the violence.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rokach |first=Ami |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9jOoDwAAQBAJ&dq=%22adam+lanza%22+aspergers&pg=PA49 |title=Senseless Violence and Its Ramifications |date=2018-10-22 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-351-60948-7 |language=en}}</ref> However, his mental health was completely untreated after 2008, leading to a "deteriorating life of dysfunction". By the time of the attack, he was severely anorexic, which medical experts believe caused cognitive impairment and may have contributed to a possible psychotic break or a "loss of touch with reality".<ref name=":5" /> A report by the Office of the Child Advocate concluded that "combined with access to deadly weapons, this proved a recipe for mass murder".{{sfn|Office of the Child Advocate|2014|p=9}}
James Knoll, a [[forensic psychiatrist]] at [[SUNY Upstate Medical University]], was consulted about what motivated Lanza to kill. Knoll states that Lanza's final act conveyed a distinct message: "I carry profound hurt—I'll go ballistic and transfer it onto you."<ref name="The Reckoning" /> 

According to the ''[[Hartford Courant]]'', there are no school records nor testimonies that Lanza was ever bullied.<ref name="courant-med-recs"/>{{rp|pp=2-3}}
According to the ''[[USA Today]]'', there are mixed anecdotes on whether Lanza was bullied or not.<ref name="stoller"/>
According to the [[New York Daily News|New York ''Daily News'']], a relative of the Lanza family claimed that Lanza was taunted and beaten by other students while he attended Sandy Hook Elementary School.<ref name="mcshane-2013">{{cite news |last1=McShane |first1=Larry |last2=Lysiak |first2=Matthew |date=April 14, 2013 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Newtown shooter Adam Lanza taunted and beaten by fellow students when he attended Sandy Hook Elementary School, relative reveals |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2013/04/14/exclusive-newtown-shooter-adam-lanza-taunted-and-beaten-by-fellow-students-when-he-attended-sandy-hook-elementary-school-relative-reveals/ |publisher=New York Daily News |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240904200342/https://www.nydailynews.com/2013/04/14/exclusive-newtown-shooter-adam-lanza-taunted-and-beaten-by-fellow-students-when-he-attended-sandy-hook-elementary-school-relative-reveals/ |archive-date=September 4, 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=September 14, 2026 |quote="Adam would come home with bruises all over his body," the relative said. "His mom would ask him what was wrong, and he wouldn't say anything. He would just sit there."}}</ref>
Amy McKinnon, the mother of one of Lanza's classmates, also alleges that Lanza was hit and teased.<ref name="averill-2013"/>
Lanza never told his parents about any bullying.<ref name="averill-2013">{{cite news |last=Averill |first=Andrew |date=April 17, 2013 |title=Adam Lanza bullied as student at Sandy Hook, his mother considered suing |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/Arts-Culture/Family/Modern-Parenthood/2013/0417/Adam-Lanza-bullied-as-student-at-Sandy-Hook-his-mother-considered-suing |publisher=The Christian Science Monitor |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260914140006/https://www.csmonitor.com/Arts-Culture/Family/Modern-Parenthood/2013/0417/Adam-Lanza-bullied-as-student-at-Sandy-Hook-his-mother-considered-suing |archive-date=September 14, 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=September 14, 2026}}</ref>
Adam's relative alleged that Nancy Lanza would come to the school with Adam each day because she believed that the school staff were failing to protect him.<ref name="mcshane-2013"/><ref name="averill-2013"/>
Nancy reputedly considered suing the school.<ref name="mcshane-2013"/><ref name="averill-2013"/>
Peter Lanza testified that Adam was bullied due to his lack of social skills and his physical gait, but not excessively.<ref name="stoller">{{cite news |last=Stoller |first=Gary |date=November 25, 2013 |title=The mystery of Adam Lanza, the Sandy Hook school gunman |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/11/25/newtown-shooting-investigation/3696425/ |location=Newtown, Connecticut |publisher=USA Today |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190225223804/https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/11/25/newtown-shooting-investigation/3696425/ |archive-date=February 25, 2019 |url-status=live |access-date=September 14, 2026}}</ref>
One of Lanza's friends during his late life in 2011 and 2012 said that Lanza never revealed being bullied in school.<ref name="stoller"/>

One theory suggests Lanza may have targeted the school because of an extreme anxiety-driven resistance to leaving his childhood home and familiar environment.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pennington |first=Carolyn |date=2014-11-21 |title=Child Advocate Report on Sandy Hook Shooting Finds Missed Opportunities |url=https://today.uconn.edu/2014/11/child-advocate-report-on-sandy-hook-shooting-finds-missed-opportunities/ |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=UConn Today |language=en-US |archive-date=October 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251014020556/https://today.uconn.edu/2014/11/child-advocate-report-on-sandy-hook-shooting-finds-missed-opportunities/ |url-status=live}}</ref>
The FBI identified Lanza's waning relationship with his mother as a considerable stressor and hardship in his life.<ref name="providence-journal-2017"/>
Nancy Lanza's desire to sell the house where she and Adam lived may have been a partial motive for the shooting, as it would have required evicting Adam from his bedroom.{{sfn|Office of the Child Advocate|2014|p=103}}<ref name="katersky-2014"/>
In the weeks leading up to the shooting, Lanza's mother contemplated moving with Adam to either Washington or North Carolina.<ref name="seattle-times-2012">{{cite news |title=Nancy Lanza had considered moving with her son to Washington state |last1=Tate |first1=Julie |last2=Crites |first2=Alice R. |url=http://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/nancy-lanza-had-considered-moving-with-her-son-to-washington-state-friend-says/ |newspaper=[[The Seattle Times]] |date=December 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170824053834/http://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/nancy-lanza-had-considered-moving-with-her-son-to-washington-state-friend-says/ |archive-date=August 24, 2017 |url-status=live |access-date=August 24, 2017}}</ref>
Nancy planned to purchase a [[recreational vehicle]] for Adam to stay in so that potential purchasers could see the house without disturbing him.{{sfn|Office of the Child Advocate|2014|p=103}}<ref name="stoller"/>
The Report of the Child Advocate stated that:
{{blockquote|In the wake of Mrs Lanza's stated plan to move out of Newtown in 2012, and perhaps stimulated by fears of leaving the "[[comfort zone]]" of his home, Adam planned and executed the massacre at Sandy Hook Elementary School on December 14, 2012.{{sfn|Office of the Child Advocate|2014|p=8}}}}

An online acquaintance told the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] (FBI) that Lanza felt pity for children, believing they were being improperly controlled by parents and teachers. She suspected Lanza may have viewed the killings as a way of saving or protecting them.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-10-25 |title=Sandy Hook shootings: Four things revealed by FBI files |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-41749336 |access-date=2026-02-08 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB |archive-date=February 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260203230336/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-41749336 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EqVhswEACAAJ |title=The Sandy Hook Shooting: The FBI Files: Unsealed Files on Adam Lanza & The Sandy Hook Shooting |date=2018-01-18 |publisher=For Our Sun Publishing |isbn=978-0-9862752-2-7 |language=en}}</ref> According to the acquaintance, Lanza wrote that he liked the ''[[Harry Potter]]'' series, especially how "at the age of 11, the kids were taken away from their families".<ref name="providence-journal-2017"/>

Suicide could have been a primary motive. Langman wrote that "Lanza was profoundly unhappy about being alive".<ref name="langman-2024"/> In a computer document, Lanza once wrote "killing yourself would intuitively be moral because you would not have the capacity to commit immoral deeds, which you innately do through being alive; and yet many would somehow forbid suicide as being immoral".<ref name="courant-spreadsheet"/>

'''Fábio Aguiar da Silva''' (born 28 February 1989) is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Agremiação Sportiva Arapiraquense|ASA]].

==Career==

===Yokohama F. Marinos===
In 2013 Fábio signed for Japanese [[J. League Division 1]] side [[Yokohama F. Marinos]] for the season and he made his debut for the club on 20 March 2013 in the [[J. League Cup]] against [[Kawasaki Frontale]] in which he started and played the full 90 as Yokohama went on to win the match 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=YOKOHAMA F. MARINOS VS. '''Muna''' (stylized in [[all caps]] as '''MUNA'''; {{ipac-en|ˈ|m|uː|n|ə}} {{respell|MOON|ə}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xModLBUY9uQ|title=4 Things About Muna You Should Know!|publisher=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|via=[[YouTube]]|date=August 13, 2019|access-date=March 22, 2021}}</ref>) is an American [[indie pop]] band consisting of [[Katie Gavin]], Josette Maskin, and Naomi McPherson. They released two studio albums with [[RCA Records]], ''[[About U]]'' (2017) and ''[[Saves the World]]'' (2019), before signing with independent label [[Saddest Factory Records]], which released their third studio album, [[Muna (Muna album)|''Muna'']], in June 2022, and ''[[Dancing on the Wall]]'' in May 2026.

== Career ==
=== 2013–2019: Career beginnings, ''About U'' and ''Saves the World'' ===
Based in [[Los Angeles]], the trio met in college at the [[University of Southern California]] and began working together in 2013 with Maskin and McPherson playing together on guitars and Gavin adding synth bass and vocals. Gavin had introduced McPherson to Maskin.<ref name="Hot Enough To Go For It w/ Muna">Las Culturistas with Matt Rogers and Bowen Yang, "[https://open.spotify.com/episode/5mQ4U2UVfhRtvUPGOAxWlH?si=e671a1e46eef47db Hot Enough To Go For It (w/ Muna)]", July 20, 2022</ref> Gavin and Maskin were music majors, while McPherson double-majored in narrative studies and American studies & ethnicity.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Stone |first=Avery |date=May 10, 2016 |title=If We're Lucky Enough to Have a Platform, We Should Use That to Help People |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/muna-on-their-own-terms-interview/ |website=Vice |language=en-US |access-date=December 11, 2022}}</ref> The two guitarists, Maskin and McPherson, had been used to playing [[ska]] and [[progressive rock]], but settled on a different sound when their initial collaboration with singer Gavin resulted in a pop song.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |last=Savage |first=Mark |title=Muna interview: Defiant pop from LA rising stars |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-37476668 |website=BBC |language=en-GB |date=September 28, 2016 |access-date=December 11, 2022}}</ref>

Beginning their collaboration in an experimental mode, they evolved towards hooky [[electronic pop]]. In the summer of 2014, they self-released their debut EP, ''More Perfect'', on [[Bandcamp]] and [[SoundCloud]]. Its success led to their signing by [[RCA Records]] in the US and [[Columbia Records]] in the UK. Gavin and McPherson dated for three years and broke up shortly after being signed.<ref name="Hot Enough To Go For It w/ Muna"/> RCA released their self-produced debut major label EP, ''Loudspeaker'', in May 2016. Their debut full-length album, ''[[About U]]'', was released on February 3, 2017.

Dutch DJ/producer [[Tiësto]] remixed "Winterbreak" in May 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Muna – Winterbreak (Tiësto's Deep House Mix) |url=http://www.tiestoblog.com/muna-winterbreak-tiesto-remix/ |website=Tiëstosblog |access-date=November 18, 2016}}</ref> Muna played [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/22/arts/music/muna-band-interview.html Lollapalooza] 2016 in Chicago in July 2016,<ref>"[https://www.lollapalooza.com/artist/muna/ retrieved November 21, 2016]</ref> toured America with [[Grouplove]] in the fall of 2016, and made their late-night network television debut on November 7, 2016, on ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rettig |first=James |date=November 8, 2016 |title=Watch Muna Make Their Late-Night TV Debut With "Loudspeaker" On Jimmy Fallon |url=http://www.stereogum.com/1910142/watch-muna-make-their-late-night-tv-debut-with-loudspeaker-on-jimmy-fallon/video/ |website=Stereogum |language=en-US |access-date=November 21, 2016}}</ref> In June 2017, it was announced that the band would be the opening act on the North American and European tour dates for [[Harry Styles]]. In 2017, their song "I Know a Place" was featured in ''[[The Carmilla Movie]]'', following the original [[Carmilla (series)|web series]] based on [[Sheridan Le Fanu]]'s [[Carmilla|novella of the same name]]. In 2018, Muna was featured playing "I Know a Place" live in the Netflix movie ''[[Alex Strangelove]]'', which chronicles the sexual awakening of teen protagonist Alex Truelove.

In 2018, the band began work on their second full-length record. In June 2019, the band announced their second album, ''[[Saves the World]]'', which was released on September 6, 2019. The album was preceded by its lead single, "Number One Fan", followed by the singles "Who", "[[Stayaway]]", and "Taken". Following their London shows at the Village Underground, it was announced that Muna would be returning to the UK for their Saves the World Tour in December 2019.<ref>{{cite instagram |author=Rᴀᴄʜ ✿ |user=dreamluminosity |date=September 11, 2019 |title=muna were so good last night, even mum enjoyed the show! #concert #muna #music |postid=B2SGFk4hkoN |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/B2SGFk4hkoN |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=registration |website=Instagram |access-date=December 11, 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

=== 2020–2024: Record label change and ''Muna'' ===
In 2020, shortly after the onset of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Muna was dropped by RCA for "not making enough money".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Bernstein |first=Jonathan |date=2022-03-15 |title=Life's So Fun: Muna Choose Happiness |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/muna-silk-chiffon-new-album-interview-1320917/ |access-date=2023-02-21 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Richards |first=Will |date=2022-11-25 |title=MUNA discuss the "creative freedom" given to them on Phoebe Bridgers' label |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/muna-discuss-the-creative-freedom-given-to-them-on-phoebe-bridgers-label-3355874 |access-date=2023-02-21 |website=NME |language=en-GB}}</ref> It was then announced in May 2021 that Muna had signed with [[Saddest Factory Records]], the record label founded by [[Phoebe Bridgers]], which operates in partnership with Secretly Group's [[Dead Oceans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Sam |date=May 19, 2021 |title=Muna sign to Phoebe Bridgers' label Saddest Factory Records |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/muna-sign-to-phoebe-bridgers-label-saddest-factory-records-2944114 |website=NME |language=en-GB |access-date=May 19, 2021}}</ref> In September 2021, Muna released their single "Silk Chiffon" featuring Bridgers, their first since signing to the label. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' called it a "buoyant track with an uncharacteristically bright declaration of queer love".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Zemler |first=Emily |date=November 9, 2021 |title=Phoebe Bridgers Takes Muna to Prom With 'Silk Chiffon' on 'Corden' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/phoebe-bridgers-muna-silk-chiffon-corden-1255237/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US |access-date=November 17, 2021}}</ref> The "Silk Chiffon" music video featuring Phoebe Bridgers is a tribute to the themes and visuals of the 1990s film ''[[But I'm a Cheerleader]]''. Band member Naomi McPherson said it is "a song for kids to have their first gay kiss to".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fadel |first1=Leila |last2=Quiroz |first2=Lilly |last3=Clark |first3=Nell |title=MUNA's new album features growth and an 'astral projection anthem' |url=https://www.thecurrent.org/feature/2022/06/24/npr-band-muna-says-take-a-song-for-its-meaning-or-use-it-for-the-way-you-need-it |website=The Current |date=June 24, 2022}}</ref> The song was chosen by a number of publications for their year-end lists of 2021, including ''Rolling Stone'',<ref>{{cite magazine |title=The 50 Best Songs of 2021 |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/50-best-songs-of-2021-list-1260934/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US |date=December 6, 2021 |access-date=June 3, 2022}}</ref> ''[[Consequence of Sound]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Top 50 Songs of 2021 |url=https://consequence.net/2021/12/top-50-songs-2021-list/ |website=Consequence of Sound |language=en-US |date=December 6, 2021 |access-date=June 3, 2022}}</ref> and [[Line of Best Fit|''The Line of Best Fit'']], who ranked it at number one.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Best Songs of 2021 Ranked |url=https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/features/articles/best-songs-of-2021-ranked |website=The Line of Best Fit |access-date=June 3, 2022}}</ref> Muna later joined [[Kacey Musgraves]] on her 15-city winter tour between January and February 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jossell |first=Shar |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Kacey Musgraves Teaming Up With Muna and King Princess for 2022 Tour |url=https://www.them.us/story/kacey-musgraves-muna-king-princess-2022-tour |website=Them |language=en-US |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>

In March 2022, the band released the single "Anything But Me", and announced that their third studio album, ''[[Muna (Muna album)|Muna]]'', would be released on June 24, 2022, through Saddest Factory and Dead Oceans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kenneally |first=Cerys |date=March 15, 2022 |title=Muna announce self-titled album with new single "Anything But Me" |url=https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/latest-news/muna-announce-self-titled-album-with-new-single-anything-but-me |website=The Line of Best Fit |language=en-US |access-date=March 15, 2022}}</ref> The following month, they performed the single on the final season of ''[[The Ellen DeGeneres Show]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Garro |first=Adrian |date=April 19, 2022 |title=Muna Brings Infectious New == Artistry ==
All three members identify as [[queer]]<ref name="auto1"/> and McPherson is [[Non-binary gender|non-binary]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Naomi McPherson Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/flurtcobain/status/965453829742514176 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220526052551/https://twitter.com/flurtcobain/status/965453829742514176 |archive-date=May 26, 2022 |access-date=April 10, 2021 |website=Twitter |language=en-US}}</ref> Initially wary of being pigeonholed as a "queer band", Muna later came to embrace the opportunity to use their musical fame to help inspire younger people to be comfortable with their identities. Their songs frequently address issues of sexuality and gender. They describe one early song, "So Special", as "an anthem for the slut-shamed girls of the world who have to assert their own value."<ref name="auto1"/> According to McPherson, "It would have meant a lot to me when I was, say, 12, to know of someone in a band and think they were cool ''and'' know they were out."<ref name="auto"/> McPherson added, "I am out and I feel safe being out because the three of us are a little army for one another. I don't feel afraid to be myself. That makes me proud to be queer. That's the whole point of why we do this. We want a safe haven."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Monroe |first=Ian David |date=November 4, 2016 |title=Muna Are Pioneering a New Identity in Pop Music |url=http://vmagazine.com/article/muna-pioneering-new-identity-pop-music/ |work=V Magazine |language=en-US ?|access-date=December 11, 2022}}</ref>

When asked the meaning behind the band name, the members state it has many different meanings and it has grown to "an entity greater than all of us individually".<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=2019-11-27 |title=The Electro-Pop Band MUNA on Style and Saving the World |url=https://www.harpersbazaar.com/culture/art-books-music/a29954384/muna-saves-the-world/ |access-date=2023-10-27 |magazine=Harper's BAZAAR |language=en-US}}</ref> They cite many different languages having different translations of the word, having originally brainstormed it without much ceremony.<ref>{{Citation |title=MUNA - Number One Fan (Official Video) | date=June 6, 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wqf-U_fibV0 |access-date=2023-10-27 |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In June 2020, in honor of the 50th anniversary of the first LGBTQ [[pride parade]], ''[[Queerty]]'' named Muna among the fifty heroes "leading the nation toward equality, acceptance, and dignity for all people".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Queerty Pride50 2020 Honorees |url=https://www.queerty.com/pride50/ |website=Queerty |language=en-US |access-date=June 30, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tracer |first=Daniel |date=July 15, 2020 |title=These musicians became queer role models young fans need, and they're changing the world for good |url=https://www.queerty.com/musicians-became-queer-role-models-young-fans-need-theyre-changing-world-good-20200715 |website=Queerty |access-date=August 2, 2020}}</ref>

== Podcast ==
In June 2021, the members of Muna began hosting a podcast called ''Gayotic'', as part of the [[Headgum]] network.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The GUi-DE: MUNA's podcast and a messed up A24 movie |url=https://i-d.co/article/beau-is-afraid-uk-release-date/ |access-date=2023-07-03 |website=i-d.vice.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Arata |first=Aiden|date=2021-10-19 |title=How linking up with Phoebe Bridgers allowed MUNA to finally be heard |url=https://www.altpress.com/muna-interview-phoebe-bridgers-saddest-factory-records/ |access-date=2023-07-03 |website=Alternative Press Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Beckett |first=Tyson |title=Muna's music is queer joy exemplified |url=https://www.thepress.co.nz/a/style/350023109/muna-s-music-is-queer-joy-exemplified |access-date=2023-07-03 |website=www.thepress.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-08-31 |title=MUNA's New Album Is Joy As An Act Of Resistance |url=https://junkee.com/munas-self-titled-album-profile/340106 |access-date=2023-07-03 |website=Junkee |language=en-US}}</ref> The official description reads, in part, "Having been described by the press as 'occasionally hard-to-follow,' 'as chaotic as they are iconic,' and 'going through it,' the band MUNA started this podcast with the hope of providing not only more income, but also rare insight into the behavior of queers outside of the month of June." The podcast often features special guests, many of whom are queer, such as [[Phoebe Bridgers]], [[Lucy Dacus]], [[Julien Baker]], [[Tegan and Sara]], and [[Clea DuVall|Clea Duvall]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Headgum: Gayotic with MUNA |url=https://headgum.com/gayotic-with-muna}}</ref>

He has [[Asperger syndrome|Asperger's]], and during year 12 he was diagnosed with [[schizoid personality disorder]], [[Depression (mood)|depression]], and [[social anxiety]] which he began taking medication for.{{Cite web |last1=Johnston |last2=Bucci |first1=Chris |first2=Nino |date=9 September 2015 |title=Melbourne 'hurtcore' paedophile master Matthew Graham outed as 'Lux' |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/melbourne-hurtcore-paedophile-master-matthew-graham-outed-as-lux-20150909-gjiuga.html |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |language=en}} Despite this, he still did well on his [[Victorian Certificate of Education|VCE]] and got into [[La Trobe University]], studying [[nanotechnology]], but soon dropped out due to pressure.{{cite web |last1=Johnston |first1=Chris |title=Reviled child pornographer Matthew Graham has 'nowhere to hide', court hears |url=https://www.theage.com.au/national/victoria/reviled-child-pornographer-matthew-graham-has-nowhere-to-hide-court-hears-20160204-gmllj1.html |website=The Age |access-date=22 September 2026 |language=en |date=4 February 2016}} Graham spent most of his time in his bedroom playing [[World of Warcraft]], and would not come out of his room or interact with his parents. His parents tried to get him treatment through a psychologist for his social anxiety, but to no avail. He was also a babysitter for his neighbour's children, but no sexual abuse took place. He browsed the anonymous imageboard [[4chan]] at the same time [[Anonymous (hacker group)|Anonymous]] launched [[Operation Darknet]]. Graham was intrigued by Anonymous and curious about the [[dark web]]. Originally just wanting to get recognition and respect for his skills in technology, he ended up in child pornography spaces. == Criminal activities == === Daisy's Destruction === Around 2011-2013, there were rumours surrounding a video called "[[Daisy's Destruction]]" — a video of a 18 month old girl named Daisy, violently abused by a masked woman for sexual pleasure. Graham, being the "King of Hurtcore", decided to seek out this video to redistribute it on his "Hurt2theCore" website. He ended up contacting a person from "[[No Limits Fun]]" named "Exciteagirl"{{efn|Is said to be Liezyl Margallo{{cite web|title=Pre-Trial Brief: Scully and Margallo Case |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/354655820/PTB}}}} to make a deal with. He offered $900 for the film, but that wasn't enough and was asked for $10,000 instead. This was completely out of Graham's budget, and he wasn't planning on asking his members for money, so he had to decline. Graham managed to grab some of the film split into 4 parts, and redistributed it on his websites for free.{{Cite web |date=16 March 2016 |title=Man behind child-abuse empire behind bars |url=https://www.nine.com.au/australia-news/vic/jail-over-vic-man-s-child-abuse-empire-20160317-p5u5po.html |access-date= |website=Nine.com.au |language=en}} Graham's relationship with NLF were soured. He said on a forum,
"Those NLF guys deserved me leaking DD. They were whiny bitches,"
Anyone who claimed Daisy's Destruction wasn't real was soon proven wrong, and this film would spread out onto the greater internet. Clips of this film continue to be distributed on the [[dark web]] and the [[Clearnet (networking)|clear web]] in the present day. It is said he did this "In the name of freedom", but also for website traffic. == Notes == {{Noteslist}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Graham, Matthew David}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Date of birth missing (living people)]] [[Category:Year of birth missing (living people)]] [[Category:21st-century Australian criminals]] [[Category:La Trobe University alumni]] [[Category:Australian people convicted of child sexual abuse]] [[Category:Criminals from Melbourne]] [[Category:People with schizoid personality disorder]] [[Category:Australian people convicted of child pornography offences]] [[Category:1992 births]] {{australia-crime-bio-stub}}

'''Ryan Melissa Connaughton''' ({{Nee|'''Gareis'''}}; born November 13, 1998) is an American professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Chicago Stars FC]] of the [[National Women's Soccer League]]. She played [[college soccer]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks women's soccer|South Carolina Gamecocks]] before being selected in the [[2022 NWSL Draft]] by the [[Houston Dash]].

== Early life ==
Connaughton is originally from [[Naperville, Illinois]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2023/08/10/napervilles-ryan-gareis-embraces-home-away-from-home-with-nwsls-houston-dash-ive-completely-fallen-in-love/ | title=Naperville's Ryan Gareis embraces home away from home with NWSL's Houston Dash: 'I've completely fallen in love' | website=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=August 10, 2023 }}</ref> She attended [[Neuqua Valley High School]], where she scored the most goals for the team her freshman year. She was a member of [https://sockersfcchicago.com/ Sockers FC] and played in the [https://www.theecnl.com/ Elite Clubs National League] (ECNL) and won [[US Club Soccer|U.S. Club Soccer]]'s National Championship in 2012 & 2013.

In 2013, Connaughton attended a U15 Girls' U.S. Youth National Team Training Camp. Connaughton was a member of Illinois' [https://www.usyouthsoccer.org/olympic-development-program/ Olympic Development Program] (ODP) in 2010 and 2014. Connaughton played for the Illinois ODP team when they played in the National Championships in 2014.

==College career==
Connaughton played [[college soccer]] at [[South Carolina Gamecocks women's soccer|South Carolina]] from 2017 to 2021. She was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team after her rookie year. She went on to score 15 goals in exactly 100 games across her five-season college career.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://gamecocksonline.com/sports/wsoc/roster/player/ryan-gareis/ | title=Ryan Gareis | date=June 22, 2018 }}</ref>

==Club career==

=== Houston Dash ===
In December 2021, Connaughton was selected by the [[Houston Dash]] in the fourth round of the [[2022 NWSL Draft]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.houstondynamofc.com/houstondash/news/houston-dash-select-forward-ryan-gareis-from-south-carolina-in-nwsl-draft | title=Houston Dash select forward Ryan Gareis from South Carolina in NWSL Draft | Houston Dynamo }}</ref> On February 18, 2022, Connaughton signed a two-year contract with Houston.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.houstondynamofc.com/houstondash/news/dash-fw-ryan-gareis-signs-two-year-contract | title=Houston Dash FW Ryan Gareis signs two-year contract | Houston Dynamo }}</ref> She made 20 appearances for the Dash in the 2022 season, and was named the club's Young Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.houstondynamofc.com/houstondash/news/houston-dash-announce-2022-team-awards | title=Houston Dash announce 2022 Team Awards | Houston Dynamo }}</ref> In January 2023, she signed a contract extension with Houston.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.houstondynamofc.com/houstondash/news/houston-dash-forward-ryan-gareis-signs-contract-extension | title=Houston Dash forward Ryan Gareis signs contract extension | Houston Dynamo }}</ref>

Connaughton scored her first NWSL goal on October 18, 2025, coming off the bench to score the lone goal in Houston's 1–0 win against the [[Kansas City Current]] that ending the Current's 17-game unbeaten streak.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Houston Dash Snap Kansas City Current 17-Match Unbeaten Streak |url=https://www.houstondynamofc.com/houstondash/news/houston-dash-snap-kansas-city-current-17-match-unbeaten-streak |access-date=October 25, 2025 |website=Houston Dash FC |language=en}}</ref> At the end of 2025, Connaughton left Houston as a free agent.<ref>{{cite web |title=NWSLPA Releases List of 2026 Free Agents as Free Agency Window Opens |url=https://www.nwslplayers.com/news/nwslpa-releases-list-of-2026-free-agents-as-free-agency-window-opens |website=NWSL Players Association |access-date=December 3, 2025}}</ref> 

=== Chicago Stars ===
On December 3, 2025, the [[Chicago Stars FC|Chicago Stars]] announced that Connaughton had signed a three-year contract with the club through 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-03 |title=Chicago Stars FC Signs Forward and Naperville Native, Ryan Gareis |url=https://chicagostars.com/first-team/chicago-stars-fc-signs-forward-and-naperville-native-ryan-gareis/ |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=Chicago Stars FC |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International career==
She attended training camp with the [[United States girls' national under-15 soccer team|United States under-15 team]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web | date=August 7, 2013|url=http://www.ussoccer.com/news/u-15-girls/2013/08/u15-gnt-to-hold-training-camp-at-the-us-soccer-national-training-center.aspx| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216042354/http://www.ussoccer.com/news/u-15-girls/2013/08/u15-gnt-to-hold-training-camp-at-the-us-soccer-national-training-center.aspx| archive-date=December 16, 2013| title=U15 GNT to Hold Training Camp at the US Soccer National Training Center - U.S. Soccer}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She and [[Pat Connaughton]] announced their relationship in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite Instagram |postid=CtcXnBUO1op |user=patconnaughton |title=And if you don't know, now you know 🤞🏼 |date=2023-06-13}}</ref> In January 2024, they announced Connaughton was pregnant.<ref>{{Cite Instagram |postid=C1nRiq9vmMa |user=ryangareis |title=Life is so good.. adding a mini 24 this '24 🩵 |date=2024-01-02}}</ref> They got engaged in February 2024 and were married in June 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2024/02/21/milwaukee-bucks-pat-connaughton-engaged-to-houston-dashs-ryan-gareis/72691407007/ | title=Milwaukee Bucks' Pat Connaughton engaged to Houston Dash's Ryan Gareis }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirby |first=Hannah |title=Ex-Bucks player Pat Connaughton marries pro soccer player Ryan Gareis |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2026/06/15/ex-bucks-player-pat-connaughton-marries-chicago-stars-ryan-gareis/90560240007/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Journal Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> Their son was born in May 2024.<ref>{{Cite Instagram |postid=C6o9_YdPYHI|user=ryangareis|title=Crew Leo Connaughton 5.3.2024 🩵 We could not possibly love you more big guy!!!|date=2024-05-06}}</ref>

'''Madwa-Nika Phanord-Cadet''', better known as '''Madwa-Nika Cadet''', is a Canadian politician, who was elected to the [[National Assembly of Quebec]] in the [[2022 Quebec general election]]. She represents the riding of [[Bourassa-Sauvé]] as a member of the [[Quebec Liberal Party]].<ref>David Beauchamp, [https://journalmetro.com/actualites/elections/2920201/nouvelle-candidate-meme-resultat-pour-bourassa-sauve/ "Nouvelle candidate, même résultat pour Bourassa-Sauvé"]. As of September 7, 2024, she serves as the critic for Employment, Labour, Youth, and French Language.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Madwa-Nika Cadet - National Assembly of Québec |url=https://www.assnat.qc.ca/en/deputes/cadet-madwa-nika-19261/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250628192437/https://www.assnat.qc.ca/en/deputes/cadet-madwa-nika-19261/index.html |archive-date=2025-06-28 |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=www.assnat.qc.ca |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ray Davon Jacobs''' (January 2, 1992 – August 26, 2023), known professionally as '''August 08''', was an American musician.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sheenmagazine.com/august08-talks-new-projects-towards-the-sun-towards-the-moon-how-he-landed-at-88rising |title=August 08 Talks New Projects 'Towards The Sun,' 'Towards The Moon' |last=Ju |first=Shirley |website=Sheen Magazine |date=July 8, 2022 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://officemagazine.net/look-towards-sun-august-08 |interviewer=Kerane Marcellus |title=Look Towards the Sun with August 08 |website=[[Office Magazine]] |date=May 20, 2022 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=https://atwoodmagazine.com/emocuh-august-08-interview-music-emotional-cuh-feature |last=Mosk |first=Mitch |title="I'm forever open": August 08 dives into the stunning depths of his intimate & vulnerable 'Emotional Cuh' |website=Atwood Magazine |date=July 15, 2021 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref> He co-wrote the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' topping hit "[[I'm the One (DJ Khaled song)|I'm the One]]" by [[DJ Khaled]] featuring [[Justin Bieber]], [[Quavo]], [[Chance the Rapper]] and [[Lil Wayne]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hitsdailydouble.com/the_bside&id=329107&title=AUGUST-08-(Def-Jam) |title=AUGUST 08 (Def Jam) |website=[[Hits (magazine)|Hitsdailydouble.com]] |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life==
Jacobs grew up in [[South Los Angeles]].<ref name="Atwood">{{Cite web |url=https://www.wonderlandmagazine.com/2021/11/18/premiere-august-08-keep-me-around |title=Meet Newcomer August 08 With His New Single "Keep Me Around" |website=[[Wonderland (magazine)|Wonderlandmagazine.com]] |date=November 18, 2021 |access-date=July 1, 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.essence.com/entertainment/august-08-all-about-the-vibes-playlist |first=Kevin L. |last=Clark |title=August 08 Crafts The Perfect Playlist For Listeners Not Afraid To Tap Into Their Soft Side |publisher=[[Essence (magazine)|Essence]] |date=May 14, 2021 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref> He had two older sisters.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.redbull.com/us-en/theredbulletin/artist-august-08-breaks-out |last=Teo-Blockey |first=Celine |title=Front Man – After years of writing hits for others, South LA native AUGUST 08 is ready to set out on his own with a deeply personal sound |work=[[The Red Bulletin]] |publisher=[[Red Bull GmbH|Red Bull Media]] |date=August 29, 2019 |access-date=October 18, 2022}}</ref> Although he did not have any musical influence from his parents,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ofuPXoOfmi4 |title=Interview: August 08 On Working With His 88Rising Crew & Learning To Colour {{!}} Cool Accidents |date=June 18, 2019 |access-date=July 1, 2023 |language=en}}</ref> his introduction to music was due to his cousins. At their house, they and Jacobs used the [[digital audio workstation]] [[FL Studio|Fruity Loops]], leading Jacobs to discover a passion for music production.<ref name="Atwood"/>

==Signing with 88rising and debut==
In 2018, he signed with American music label [[88rising]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://i-d.co/article/august-08-is-set-to-be-88risings-next-breakout-star |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221013183347/https://i-d.vice.com/en/article/ne9qpk/august-08-is-set-to-be-88risings-next-breakout-star |archive-date=2022-10-13 |work=[[i-D]] |last=Wright |first=Georgie |title=August 08 is set to be 88rising's next breakout star |publisher=[[Vice (website)|Vice]] |date=April 11, 2018 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.onestowatch.com/en/blog/august-08-father-issues-live-interview |first=Maxamillion |last=Polo |title=August 08 – "Father Issues" [Live + Interview] – All Eyes On |work=[[Ones to Watch]] |date=May 22, 2019 |access-date=October 18, 2022 }}</ref> He released his debut project, ''Father'', on May 11, 2018.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=http://onestowatch.com/en/blog/august-08-father-issues-live-interview |last=Polo |first=Maxamillion |title=August 08 – "Father Issues" [Live + Interview] {{!}} All Eyes On |date=May 22, 2019 |access-date=August 9, 2024 |website=[[Ones to Watch]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Death==
August 08 was shot dead in a case of mistaken identity, after a group of Crips mistook him as a Blood over his red hat.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2025-05-08/august-08-murder-case |title=L.A. hitmaker’s red hat led accused killers to mistake him for gang rival, police say |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=August 13, 2025 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The musician's death was ruled a [[homicide]]. He died on August 26, 2023, at the age of 31.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/august-08-singer-songwriter-dead-183325850.html |title=August 08, Singer-Songwriter, Dead At 31 |date=August 29, 2023 |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=[[Yahoo]].com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.complex.com/music/a/markelibert/august-08-has-died |last=Elibert |first=Mark |title=Singer Songwriter August 08 Dead at 31 |website=[[Complex Networks|Complex.com]] |date=August 29, 2023 |access-date=January 2, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://homicide.latimes.com/post/ray-davon-jacobs |title=Ray Davon Jacobs, 31 |website=[[Los Angeles Times|Homicide.latimes.com]] |date=November 8, 2023 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref>

==Posthumous album==
His first posthumous album, ''Pretend It's Okay'', was released on August 8, 2024.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/def-jam-recordings-releases-august-08-posthumous-album-listen |last=Strauss |first=Matthew |title=Def Jam Releases August 08's Posthumous Album |website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=August 9, 2024 |access-date=August 9, 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Bracha Jaffe''' (born {{Birth based on age as of dates|33|2023|01|03|noage=y|33|2022|02|13}})<ref name=":0" /><ref name="TO" /> is an American [[Orthodox Judaism|Orthodox Jewish]] singer.

==Music career==
Jaffe began playing [[piano]] at four years old and would sing as well. She later auditioned for Malky Giniger's Voices of Youth Choir. In high school, she taught piano and gave voice lessons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grosskopf |first=Rachel |date=2012-12-28 |title=A Heart Full Of Song: Bracha Jaffe |url=http://www.5tjt.com/a-heart-full-of-song-bracha-jaffe/ |access-date=2025-01-21 |website=[[Five Towns Jewish Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Jaffe began performing for local women’s events as a pregnant newlywed in [[nursing school]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chizhik-Goldschmidt |first=Avital |date=2021-04-12 |title=Orthodox Jewish Women Can’t Sing In Front of Men. Instagram Is Giving Them a Voice |url=https://www.glamour.com/story/orthodox-jewish-women-are-barred-from-singing-in-front-of-men-instagram-is-changing-that |access-date=2025-01-21 |website=[[Glamour (magazine)|Glamour]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In line with [[Tzniut#Female singing voice|Orthodox Jewish law]], Jaffe sings only with an all-female band and plays only for all-female audiences.  She also makes her [[social media]] accounts available only for female visitors.<ref name="TO"/>

==2023 concert ban controversy==
Jaffe was scheduled to perform in concert on January 15, 2023 at [[Hackney Empire]] in London. In late 2022, various religious authorities banned girls from local Jewish schools from attending the event, and the Vaad L'maan Tohar Machneinu ("group for the purity of our camp") branch of the [[Union of Orthodox Hebrew Congregations]] (UOHC) stated they "[endorse] and [support] this decision" to ban the concert, citing fears of "spiritual harm in ''ruchniyus'' [spirituality] and ''[[hashkafa]]'' [Jewish ethos]".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Decker |first=Adam |date=2023-01-03 |title=Anger and confusion as strictly-Orthodox girls banned from London concert |url=https://www.jewishnews.co.uk/bracha-jaffe-concert-ban/ |access-date=2025-01-21 |website=[[Jewish News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Mosheim |first=Tash |title=Bracha Jaffe’s concert banned by Orthodox rabbis sells out after woman defy prohibition |url=https://www.thejc.com/news/concert-shunned-by-orthodox-rabbis-sells-out-after-women-defy-boycott-xih6fazh |access-date=2025-01-21 |website=[[The Jewish Chronicle]] |language=en}}</ref> In response, Jaffe said "Our girls need healthy [[Kashrut|kosher]] music, healthy kosher entertainment that will bring them closer to God. [...] I only want to be a positive role model.".<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In a video message, she said that she was "greatly saddened" by the controversy but nevertheless hoped to have "an emotional and spiritual connection" with fans at the concert.<ref name=":0" /> Reportedly, some women only attended the concert after hearing about the ban.<ref name=":1" />

==Personal life==
Jaffe was raised in [[Borough Park, Brooklyn|Borough Park]], Brooklyn, New York City, and lives there with her husband and five children. For a time, she lived in [[Far Rockaway]].<ref name="TO">{{Cite web |last=Steinberg |first=Jessica |title=Religious singer Bracha Jaffe books Jerusalem hall for women only |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/religious-singer-bracha-jaffe-books-jerusalem-hall-for-women-only/ |access-date=2025-01-21 |website=[[Times of Israel]] |language=en-US}}</ref>  

Jaffe practiced for several years as a [[nurse practitioner]], until she left in September 2022.<ref name="TO" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eller |first=Sandy |date=2025-10-01 |title=Q&A: Bracha Jaffe on Music, Women-Only Concerts and Inspiring the Next Generation |url=https://jewishlink.news/qa-bracha-jaffe-on-music-women-only-concerts-and-inspiring-the-next-generation/ |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=The Jewish Link |language=en}}</ref>

Per [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style#Current|WP:MOS]], [[MOS:CURRENT]], [[MOS:REALTIME]], and [[WP:PW]] consensus, do not use terms like "current" and "currently". -->, she is signed to [[WWE]], where she performs on the [[SmackDown (WWE brand)|SmackDown]] brand under the [[ring name]] '''Tatum Paxley''' and is one-half of the reigning [[WWE Women's Tag Team Championship]] alongside [[Alexa Bliss]] in their first reign. She is also a former [[List of NXT Women's Champions|one-time]] [[NXT Women's Champion]] and a former one-time [[NXT Women's North American Champion]], and the second woman (after [[Stephanie Vaquer]]) to win both championships.

Prior to becoming a professional wrestler, Holland was a successful [[powerlifter]], winning the USA Powerlifting (USAPL) championship multiple times.

== Early life ==
Natalie Elizabeth Holland was born on October 29, 1996 in [[Dallas, Texas]].<ref name="bd"/> Holland's athletic experience includes [[cheerleading]] and [[powerlifting]].<ref name="cagematch">{{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=25037|title=Tatum Paxley|first=Philip|last=Kreikenbohm|publisher=Cagematch – The Internet Wrestling Database|access-date=February 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250825152028/https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=25037|archive-date=August 25, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> She is a former two-time USA Powerlifting (USAPL) champion, winning competitions in 2019 and 2021.<ref name="TX Lifter T. Paxley">[https://usapl.liftingdatabase.com/lifters-view?id=55274 Natalie Holland]'s Profile at USAPL Lifting Database.com. Retrieved May 8, 2026.</ref>

On October 14 episode of NXT, Paxley won a battle royal to become the No. 1 contender for the NXT Women's Championship by last eliminating Dame and [[Jordynne Grace]], with her former tag team partner Lyra Valkyria joining the ring to celebrate with her, seemingly reverting Paxley to a tweener in the process.<ref name="NXT10142025">{{cite web|last=Moore|first=John|title=NXT TV results (10/14): Moore's review of a battle royal for a shot at the NXT Women's Title at the Halloween Havoc, Matt Cardona vs. Josh Briggs, Blake Monroe vs. Zaria|url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2025/10/14/nxt-tv-results-10-14-moores-review-of-a-battle-royal-for-a-shot-at-the-nxt-womens-title-at-the-halloween-havoc-matt-cardona-vs-josh-briggs-blake-monroe-vs-zaria/|date=October 14, 2025|work=[[Pro Wrestling Dot Net]]|access-date=October 16, 2025}}</ref> At [[NXT Halloween Havoc (2025)|Halloween Havoc]] on October 25, Paxley defeated Jayne to win the title.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |title=Tatum Paxley Makes History Beating Jacy for 1st NXT Women's Title at Halloween Havoc |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25263507-tatum-paxley-makes-history-beating-jacy-1st-nxt-womens-title-halloween-havoc |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref> At the subsequent episode of ''NXT'', Paxley went against the advice of Dame and reintroduced The Wheel with contenders from NXT and [[Evolve (WWE brand)|Evolve]]. With Dame's name noticeably missing, [[Lola Vice]] was chosen to be the next No. 1 Contender. The match ended in [[Disqualification (professional wrestling)|disqualification]] as they tried to fend off Fatal Influence after Dame was ambushed. The following week on ''NXT'', the duo of Paxley and Dame, alongside Vice, lost to [[Fatal Influence]] in a [[six-woman tag team match]], making Paxley reconsider her stance of being a fighting champion; on the behest of Dame, the following week Paxley would give Jayne her rematch, on the promise that Jayne can never challenge for the title again, if she were to lose. At [[NXT Gold Rush (2025)|NXT Gold Rush]] on November 18, Paxley lost the title back to Jayne after Dame turned on her, ending her reign at 24 days, marking the shortest reign in the title's history, exiling Paxley from The Culling, and cementing her face turn.

===== NXT Women's North American Champion (2026) =====
At [[NXT Deadline (2025)|NXT Deadline]], Paxley was defeated by Dame due to distraction from her former stable. Paxley would then get her revenge on Dame by defeating her at [[NXT: New Year's Evil (2026)|''NXT'': New Year's Evil]]<ref name="NXTNYE2026">{{cite web|last=Moore|first=John|date=January 6, 2026|title=NXT TV results (1/6): Moore's review of New Year's Evil with Oba Femi vs. Leon Slater for the NXT Championship, Jacy Jayne vs. Kendal Grey for the NXT Women's Championship|url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2026/01/06/nxt-tv-results-1-6-moores-review-of-new-years-evil-with-oba-femi-vs-leon-slater-for-the-nxt-championship-jacy-jayne-vs-kendal-grey-for-the-nxt-womens-championship/|access-date=January 6, 2026|work=[[Pro Wrestling Dot Net]]}}</ref> and by dethroning her to become the new NXT Women's North American Champion at [[NXT Vengeance Day (2026)|NXT Vengeance Day]].<ref name="NXTVengeanceDay2026">{{cite web|last=Moore|first=John|title=NXT Vengeance Day results: Moore's live review of Joe Hendry vs. Ricky Saints for the NXT Championship, Izzi Dame vs. Tatum Paxley for the NXT Women's North American Championship,making her the second superstar alongside Stephanie Vaquer to hold both the NXT women’s Championship and the North American Championship.|url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2026/03/07/nxt-vengeance-day-results-moores-live-review-of-joe-hendry-vs-ricky-saints-for-the-nxt-championship-izzi-dame-vs-tatum-paxley-for-the-nxt-womens-north-american-championship/|date=March 7, 2026|work=[[Pro Wrestling Dot Net]]|access-date=March 7, 2026}}</ref> With the win, she became the second woman after [[Stephanie Vaquer]] to win both NXT Women's Championship and NXT Women's North American Championship. On the March 17 episode of ''NXT'', Paxley retained the title against Dame inside a steel cage match to end their feud. After the match, Paxley was attacked by [[Mariah May|Blake Monroe]] with Monroe stealing her title.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wannan |first=Jack |date=March 17, 2026 |title=WWE NXT 3/17 Results: Blake Monroe attacks Tatum Paxley following successful title win, Wren Sinclair captures Speed belt |url=https://www.postwrestling.com/2026/03/17/wwe-nxt-3-17-results-blake-monroe-attacks-tatum-paxley-following-successful-title-win-wren-sinclair-captures-speed-belt/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=[[POST Wrestling]] |language=}}</ref>
At [[NXT Stand & Deliver (2026)|NXT Stand & Deliver]], Paxley retained the title against Monroe. In a rematch for the title at Week 2 of ''NXT'': Revenge on April 21, Paxley defeated Monroe in a casket match. The match was notable to be the first casket match for a championship since the [[Royal Rumble (1998)|1998 Royal Rumble]] between [[The Undertaker]] and [[WWE Championship|WWF Champion]] [[Shawn Michaels]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore|first=John|date=April 21, 2026|title=NXT TV results (4/21): Moore's review of NXT Revenge week two with Sol Ruca vs. Zaria in a Last Woman Standing match, Myles Borne vs. Dion Lennox for the NXT North American Championship|url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2026/04/21/nxt-tv-results-4-21-moores-review-of-nxt-revenge-week-two-with-sol-ruca-vs-zaria-in-a-last-woman-standing-match-myles-borne-vs-dion-lennox-for-the-nxt-north-american-championship/|access-date=April 22, 2026|website=Pro Wrestling Dot Net|language=}}</ref> On the June 9 episode of ''NXT'', she lost the NXT Women's North American Championship to Zaria, ending her reign at 94 days.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Powell |first1=Jason |title=NXT TV results (6/9): Moore's review of Kelani Jordan vs. Kendal Grey for a shot at the NXT Women's Title, Naraku vs. Mason Rook for a shot at the NXT Championship |url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2026/06/09/nxt-tv-results-6-9-moores-review-of-kelani-jordan-vs-kendal-grey-for-a-shot-at-the-nxt-womens-title-naraku-vs-mason-rook-for-a-shot-at-the-nxt-championship/ |website=Pro Wrestling Dot Net |access-date=June 10, 2026 |date=June 9, 2026}}</ref> At [[NXT The Great American Bash (2026)|NXT The Great American Bash]] on June 28, Paxley failed to regain the title from Zaria. On the June 30 episode of ''NXT'', Paxley wrestled against [[Kelani Jordan]] in a losing effort in what would be her final match in NXT.

'''Hugo Axell Ancajima Effio''' is a Peruvian professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for [[Peruvian Primera División|Peruvian Liga 1]] club [[ADC Juan Pablo II College]].

== Career ==
Ancajima played in the youth ranks of [[Universidad San Martín]] from 2013 to 2015. In 2015, he moved to [[Sporting Cristal]] and, in 2016, he started playing in its reserves, originally as a right winger, being part of the team that won the [[2016 Torneo de Promoción y Reserva]] and a starter in the team which ended as a runner up in the [[2017 Torneo de Promoción y Reserva|2017 edition]].

In August 2018, after not being given opportunities to be promoted to the first team in Cristal, Ancajima was signed by [[Cienciano]] for one season and a half.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fernández |first=Rogger |date=2 August 2018 |title=Cienciano del Cusco ficha a joven promesa de Sporting Cristal |language=Spanish |trans-title=Cienciano del Cusco signs young promise from Sporting Cristal |work=El Bocón |url=https://elbocon.pe/futbol-peruano/descentralizado/futbolista-sporting-cristal-cienciano-copa-sudamericana-171181/ |access-date=17 November 2023}}</ref> He made his professional debut in a match against [[Unión Huaral]] and played regularly that semester, in a total of 14 matches. In 2019, he was part of the team that won the [[2019 Liga 2 (Peru)|2019 Liga 2]]; however, he did not play regularly anymore, since Sebastián Lojas was the starter in his position during nearly the whole season.

In November 2020, Ancajima was signed by [[Pirata F.C.|Pirata]], but did not play a single game there. In February 2021, he was signed by [[Cultural Santa Rosa]], where he was reconverted into a right-back by manager Gustavo Cisneros<ref>{{Cite news |last=Maraví |first=Jean Pierre |date=14 June 2021 |title=Hugo Ancajima: su historia, el gol ante Alianza Lima y la estrategia de su equipo para avanzar en la Copa Bicentenario |language=Spanish |trans-title=Hugo Ancajima: his story, the goal against Alianza Lima and his team's strategy to advance in the Copa Bicentenario |work=Trome |url=https://trome.com/deportes/hugo-ancajima-su-historia-el-gol-ante-alianza-lima-y-la-estrategia-de-su-equipo-para-avanzar-en-la-copa-bicentenario-noticia/ |access-date=17 November 2023}}</ref> and became a key player in the team that reached the final stages of the [[2021 Liga 2 (Peru)|Liga 2]], without achieving promotion.

In 2022, Ancajima was signed by [[Asociación Deportiva Tarma]] to play in the [[2022 Liga 1 (Peru)|2022 Liga 1]], where he became the undisputed starter for right-back and stood out in many matches. In November 2022, after his contract with ADT finished, he was formally announced as a new signing of [[Universitario de Deportes]], with a 2-season contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2022 |title=Hugo Ancajima fue oficializado como nuevo jugador de Universitario por 2 temporadas |trans-title=Hugo Ancajima was formally announced as a new player of Universitario for 2 seasons |url=https://ovacion.pe/noticias/universitario/hugo-ancajima-fue-oficializado-nuevo-jugador-universitario-2-temporadas |access-date=17 November 2023 |website=Ovación}}</ref> Ancajima arrived on request by sporting director [[Manuel Barreto]], who knew him from his time working in the youth ranks of [[Sporting Cristal]]. He played his first game with ''la U'' on matchday 3 of the [[2023 Liga 1 (Peru)|2023 Liga 1]], in a 4–0 victory against [[Academia Cantolao]], with Ancajima being one of the players who stood out the most. After the arrival of manager [[Jorge Fossati]], he began playing as a [[right wing-back]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mauricio |first=Alberto |date=29 April 2023 |title=Golazo de taco de Alex Valera y triplete en el Universitario vs Sport Boys por Liga 1 |trans-title=Great backheel goal from Alex Valera and hat-trick in Universitario vs Sport Boys for the Liga 1 |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2023/04/29/gol-y-triplete-alex-valera-universitario-vs-sport-boys-liga-1-hoy-video/ |access-date=28 April 2024 |website=[[Infobae]] |language=Spanish}}</ref> becoming the usual substitute of [[Andy Polo]].

'''Anahí Fernández''' (born 28 July 1993) is a Uruguayan football referee. She has officiated at the international level under the auspices of [[FIFA]] and [[CONMEBOL]] and was selected as one of the officials for the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]] in Australia and [[New Zealand]].

Fernández began her refereeing career in Uruguay and steadily rose through the ranks of domestic and regional football. She was listed as an international referee by [[FIFA]], allowing her to officiate in international tournaments.

She gained experience in a number of [[CONMEBOL]] and [[FIFA]] competitions, including matches in the [[Copa Libertadores Femenina]] and international friendlies. She has overseen numerous international fixtures across various competitions, including youth and senior level matches for both men’s and women’s teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anahí Fernandez - Matches as referee |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe877076/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=worldfootball.net |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Fernández was selected to officiate at the FIFA Women’s [[World cup|World Cup]] in Australia and New Zealand. She was one of the few South American referees included in the tournament's officiating pool, a distinction noted in media coverage of her appointment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-09 |title=FIFA designó a la uruguaya Anahí Fernández para dirigir el Mundial femenino 2023 |url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/mundial/nota/_/id/11455058/anahi-fernandez-uruguaya-arbitra-copa-del-mundo-femenina-australia-nueva-zelanda-2023-fifa |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=ESPNdeportes.com |language=es}}</ref> Though she served primarily in supporting roles during the group stage, her participation represented a milestone for Uruguayan refereeing on the global stage.

Fernández has also officiated in South American women's competitions, including [[World cup|World Cup]] qualifying matches and continental tournaments.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SoccerWay A. Fernández |url=https://el.soccerway.com/referees/anahi-fernandez-hernandez/801279/}}</ref>

Moses grew up as a [[Vegetarianism|vegetarian]].{{cite web |last1=Seabrook III |first1=Robby |title=The Break Presents – Bizzy Banks |url=https://www.xxlmag.com/bizzy-banks-interview-the-break/ |website=XXL Mag |access-date=4 September 2025}} Moses states his brother is his biggest inspiration for making music.{{cite web |title=Bizzy Banks Is Ready to Take Over the Brooklyn Drill Scene |url=https://djbooth.net/features/2020-10-14-bizzy-banks-interview-brooklyn-drill-audiomack/ |website=DJ Booth |access-date=4 September 2025}} In an interview with DJ Booth in 2020, Moses stated "My older brother and my father going to jail when I was younger, it just made me become older at a young age because those two were the only two males in the house really...It was [just] me and my mom after a while. '''Miguel Corral Torreira''' ([[A Coruña|La Coruña]], 10 July 1991) is a Spanish football manager who is the head coach of the [[Botswana Premier League]] club [[Mochudi Centre Chiefs SC|Mochudi Centre Chiefs]].

After coaching youth sides in [[Galicia (Spain)]], he travelled to [[Panama]] and was assistant coach in [[Herrera FC]] before being appointed manager of the team in 2022. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2023/11/13/gallego-miguel-corral-entrenador-revelacion-futbol-panameno/00031699894649951819915.htm|title=El gallego Miguel Corral, entrenador revelación del fútbol panameño|publisher=La Voz de Galicía|language=es|date=15 November 2023|access-date=4 October 2025}}</ref> On 27 November 2023, two days after leaving Herrera, he was appointed manager of fellow [[Liga Panameña de Fútbol]] club [[UMECIT FC]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/migrantes_del_balon/panama-es-un-pais-pequeno-pero-con-mucho-talento-individual-n/|title=“Panamá es un país pequeño, pero con mucho talento individual”|publisher=Diario AS|language=es|date=12 June 2025|access-date=4 October 2025}}</ref> He left in June 2025 and signed for [[Super League Kerala]] side [[Malappuram FC|Malappuram]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://footem.in/malappuram-fc-appoints-new-coach-miguel-corral/|title=Malappuram FC Hires New Coach Miguel Corral for Super League Kerala|publisher=footem.in|language=en|date=3 August 2025|access-date=4 October 2025}}</ref> He left the club on 22 November 2025.

On 9 January 2026 he was appointed manager of [[Mochudi Centre Chiefs]] in the [[Botswana Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mochudicentrechiefs.com/2026/01/09/miguel-corral-torreira-appointed-head-coach-of-mochudi-centre-chiefs/|title=Miguel Corral Torreira Appointed Head Coach of Mochudi Centre Chiefs|publisher=mochudicentrechiefs.com|language=en|date=9 January 2026|access-date=20 February 2026}}</ref>

'''Leni Gruber''' (born 1991) is an [[Austria]]n [[film director]] and [[screenwriter]].

==Life and career==
Gruber grew up in Wels and became active early in the local cultural scene around the Alter Schlachthof Wels and the Media Culture House.
In 2012 she began studying screenwriting & dramaturgy and production at the Film Academy Vienna.<ref>{{cite web|author=Cinema Next|url=https://thegap.at/interview-leni-gruber-alex-reinberg-hollywood/|title=Last Straw: Victim Roles in Fire Drills – Leni Gruber and Alex Reinberg on "Hollywood"|work=The Gap|date=5 April 2023|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cinemanext.at/portraets/leni-gruber|title=Leni Gruber – Author and Director|work=Cinema Next|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref>

She has made several short films that have screened at national and international festivals, including the [[Sarajevo Film Festival]], Crossing Europe Film Festival Linz, YOUKI and the [[Max Ophüls]] Prize Film Festival.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fm4.orf.at/stories/2901213/|title=Unpredictable and Tender|work=FM4|date=15 March 2018|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diagonale.at/filmarchiv/|title=Film Archive|work=Diagonale – Festival of Austrian Film|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref>
Her films often explore everyday realities and are noted for their subtle humour. In interviews, Gruber has described her work as a search for authenticity in both performance and direction.

She has also served as a jury member, including for the short film competition at the [[Diagonale]] – Festival of Austrian Film and at the Kürzestfilm Festival.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diagonale.at/jury-kurzspielfilm-23/|title=Short Film Jury 2023|work=Diagonale – Festival of Austrian Film|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/3000000225124/kuerzestfilm-festspiele-im-gartenbaukino-zwoelf-sekunden-anarchie|title=Kürzestfilm Festival at Gartenbaukino: Twelve Seconds of Anarchy|work=Der Standard|language=de-AT|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Les Nouveaux Riches Magazine|url=https://www.les-nouveaux-riches.com/landjaeger-kuerzestfilm-festspiele/|title=Kürzestfilm Festspiele 2024|date=15 May 2024|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://fm4.orf.at/stories/3028101/|title=Young Film Culture and Meme Competence at Youki in Wels|work=FM4|date=10 October 2022|language=de|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref>

==Filmography==

* 2018: Schneemann – short film (20 min)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.refreshingfilms.com/filme/hollywood/standard-titel|title=LEMONADE FILMS – Leni Gruber & Alex Reinberg|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2022: Hollywood – short film, co-directed with Alex Reinberg<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wt1.at/news/leni-gruber-mit-ihrem-erfolgsfilm-hollywood/|title=Leni Gruber – With Her Successful Film "Hollywood"|work=WT1|access-date=17 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2026: Sheep – short series (5 episodes, 20min each), co-directed with Alex Reinberg<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pressemappe |url=https://presseportal.zdf.de/pressemappe/sheep |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=ZDF Presseportal |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-29 |title=Sprechende Schafe zum Sommerkinoauftakt in Waidhofen/Ybbs |url=https://www.noen.at/ybbstal/kino-unter-sternen-sprechende-schafe-zum-sommerkinoauftakt-in-waidhofen-ybbs-532732819 |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=www.noen.at |language=de}}</ref>
