'''Matheus Bazzo Malgarise''' (born 29 October 1990 in [[Passo Fundo]]) is a Brazilian designer, photographer, producer, art director and entrepreneur. Bazzo is the producer of the movie {{lang|pt|O Jardim das Aflições}} {{gloss|The Garden of Afflictions}}, which depicts the work, thoughts and daily life of Brazilian philosopher and writer [[Olavo de Carvalho]] (1947–2022). He is also the founder of Lumine, a Catholic [[Streaming media|streaming]] platform, as well as of [[Minha Biblioteca Católica]] (My Catholic Library), a religious book subscription club.

== Career ==
Born in the city of Passo Fundo, in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, Bazzo resided only for a short time in his own native city and moved to [[São Leopoldo]] with his family, to the region of Vale dos Sinos. At 16 he started experimenting with analog photography, having launched a [[zine]] called Câmera Diynamite<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gloria |first=Rafael |date=24 April 2012 |title=Camera Diynamite lança o primeiro Zine |url=https://www.nonada.com.br/2012/04/camera-diynamite-lanca-o-primeiro-zine/ |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Nonada Jornalismo |language=pt-BR |archive-date=17 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251217123627/https://www.nonada.com.br/2012/04/camera-diynamite-lanca-o-primeiro-zine/ |url-status=live }}</ref>, which published pictures shot by artists from around the world. In the aftermath, he began his undergraduate studies in [[Visual arts|Visual Arts]] at [[Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul]]. At the time he worked as a photographer and also as a designer, acting in companies of the sector and collaborating with press vehicles such as [[Vice Media|Vice]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matheus Bazzo |url=https://www.vice.com/pt/topic/matheus-bazzo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240302131826/https://www.vice.com/pt/topic/matheus-bazzo |archive-date=2 March 2024 |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=www.vice.com |language=pt}}</ref>. 

In the year of 2011 Bazzo was introduced to the work of Olavo de Carvalho, and from the philosopher's ideas he conceptualized the movie ''O Jardim das Aflições'', in order to present the life and daily routine of that Brazilian thinker. Matheus Bazzo later joined with director [[Josias Teófilo]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 July 2016 |title=Cineasta cria documentário baseado na obra filosófica de Olavo de Carvalho |url=https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/app/noticia/diversao-e-arte/2016/07/19/interna_diversao_arte,540843/cineasta-cria-documentario-baseado-na-obra-filosofica-de-olavo-de-carv.shtml |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Acervo |publisher=[[Correio Braziliense]] |language=pt-BR |archive-date=12 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251212141714/https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/app/noticia/diversao-e-arte/2016/07/19/interna_diversao_arte,540843/cineasta-cria-documentario-baseado-na-obra-filosofica-de-olavo-de-carv.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> who had a similar project in mind. The partnership began when they jointly started developing this project. 

Between 2015 and 2016, Matheus Bazzo and Josias Teófilo fundraised for the documentary in what was the biggest [[crowdfunding]] in Brazil's history<ref>{{Cite web |title=Financiamento coletivo leva mais uma produção às telas de cinema com quebra de recorde de arrecadação |url=https://www.terra.com.br/noticias/financiamento-coletivo-leva-mais-uma-producao-as-telas-de-cinema-com-quebra-de-recorde-de-arrecadacao,c4f48d3da41fb7524b2588cf85c1243d64pgry02.html |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Terra |language=pt-BR |agency=Dino |archive-date=27 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227120117/https://www.terra.com.br/noticias/financiamento-coletivo-leva-mais-uma-producao-as-telas-de-cinema-com-quebra-de-recorde-de-arrecadacao,c4f48d3da41fb7524b2588cf85c1243d64pgry02.html |url-status=live }}</ref>, a fundraising valued at R$ 350.000,00 among 2.800 individual investors. The shooting took place in the year of 2015, in the [[United States]], in [[Richmond, Virginia]]. The film premiere was held on 31 May 2017,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Em meio à controvérsia, documentário “O Jardim das Aflições” tem pré-estreia amanhã (31), em cinco capitais |url=https://www.mundodomarketing.com.br/noticias-corporativas/conteudo/131630/em-meio-a-controversia-documentario-o-jardim-das-aflicoes-tem-pre-estreia-amanha-31-em-cinco-capitais |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221013043821/https://www.mundodomarketing.com.br/noticias-corporativas/conteudo/131630/em-meio-a-controversia-documentario-o-jardim-das-aflicoes-tem-pre-estreia-amanha-31-em-cinco-capitais |archive-date=13 October 2022 |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Mundo do Marketing |language=pt-BR |department=Notícias Corporativas}}</ref> and had a great repercussion in mainstream media primarily due to differences between Olavo's supporters and opponents<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prisco |first=Luiz |date=14 May 2017 |title=Protesto contra filmes de "direita" faz Cine PE ser adiado |url=https://www.metropoles.com/entretenimento/cinema/protesto-contra-filmes-de-direita-faz-cine-pe-ser-adiado |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=www.metropoles.com |language=pt-BR}}</ref>. That same year, ''O Jardim das Aflições'' won the award for best picture and film editing in the 21st Cine-PE Festival.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 July 2017 |title=Documentário pernambucano sobre filósofo Olavo de Carvalho vence o 21º Cine PE |url=https://g1.globo.com/pernambuco/noticia/documentario-pernambucano-sobre-filosofo-olavo-de-carvalho-vence-o-21-cine-pe.ghtml |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=G1 |language=pt-br |archive-date=8 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208222439/https://g1.globo.com/pernambuco/noticia/documentario-pernambucano-sobre-filosofo-olavo-de-carvalho-vence-o-21-cine-pe.ghtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

During 2017, Bazzo undertakes a personal project, Minha Biblioteca Católica (MBC), a book subscription club for Catholic readers that printed more than seven million books<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 February 2026 |title=Projeto editorial gaúcho expande atuação para os EUA |url=https://gauchazh.clicrbs.com.br/colunistas/rodrigo-lopes/noticia/2026/02/projeto-editorial-gaucho-expande-atuacao-para-os-eua-cml6q38dd00kc015btn82h2pk.html |access-date=3 February 2026 |website=GZH |language=pt}}</ref>, including great religious classics such as ''The'' ''Story of a Soul'', by [[Thérèse of Lisieux]], ''Theology of the Body'', by [[Pope John Paul II]], as well as ''The Interior Castle'', by [[Teresa of Ávila]]. 

In November 2023, after three years of work, the company launched a groundbreaking edition of the [[Bible|Holy Bible]], a revised translation of Father Matos Soares' 1927 work, based on the [[Vulgate]] – the most traditional version of Scripture in the Catholic Church, with references to manuscripts and versions in [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] and [[Greek language|Greek]].<ref name="JC_2024">{{Cite web |date=25 November 2024 |title=Editora de Dois Irmãos vence categoria do Prêmio Jabuti |url=https://www.jornaldocomercio.com/jornal-cidades/2024/11/1180983-editora-de-dois-irmaos-vence-categoria-do-premio-jabuti.html |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Jornal do Comércio |language=pt-br}}</ref>

This version of the Bible was one of the winners of the 2024 [[Prêmio Jabuti|Jabuti Prize]] in the "Editorial Production" category, receiving the trophy for best cover.<ref name="JC_2024"/> In addition, it won two medals for "Editorial Project" at the Brazilian Design Awards<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2024 |title=Que Bíblia é essa que conquistou o Jabuti e prêmios de design |url=https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/cultura/biblia-caprichada-conquistou-jabuti-premios-design/ |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Gazeta do Povo |language=pt-BR}}</ref>. In the second half of 2025, the company began operations in the United States<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 February 2026 |title=Projeto editorial gaúcho expande atuação para os EUA |url=https://gauchazh.clicrbs.com.br/colunistas/rodrigo-lopes/noticia/2026/02/projeto-editorial-gaucho-expande-atuacao-para-os-eua-cml6q38dd00kc015btn82h2pk.html |access-date=3 February 2026 |website=GZH |language=pt}}</ref>. 

In the year of 2019, Matheus founds Lumine, a streaming platform with content designed for the Catholic audiences. That service gathers classic films of [[Charlie Chaplin|Charles Chaplin]] and [[Alfred Hitchcock]], among others, and also movies and series with religious content, including original productions made by Lumine itself. In just three years Lumine became the biggest Catholic streaming platform in [[Latin America]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 September 2021 |title=Lumine lança filme sobre Anchieta no maior evento on-line sobre cinema e religião do país - Vatican News |url=https://www.vaticannews.va/pt/igreja/news/2021-09/lumine-plataforma-catolica-filme-jose-anchieta-apostolo-brasil.html |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=www.vaticannews.va |language=pt |archive-date=19 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250319172726/https://www.vaticannews.va/pt/igreja/news/2021-09/lumine-plataforma-catolica-filme-jose-anchieta-apostolo-brasil.html |url-status=live }}</ref>. 

=== Personal life ===
Matheus converted to Catholicism in 2013. He is married with screenwriter and director Julia Sondermann since 2019 – they had three children together.

'''Naomichi Hanazono''' (Japanese: 花園 直道) is a Japanese [[:ja:舞踊|classical]] dance performer and singer.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Naomichi Hanazono – Japan Expo Malaysia |url=http://www.japanexpomalaysia.com/naomichi-hanazono/ |access-date=2025-12-21 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
He began studying classical dance in the Bandō style (Natori / Bandō Tsutayuki-ryū) as well as [[Tsugaru-jamisen|Tsugaru shamisen]] at an early age. Seeking to create an innovative form of Japanese dance with a fresh sensibility—an approach he personally termed "Japanese"—he combined traditional dance with vocal performance. In 2006, he formed the dance group Kabuto, and their performances have since been warmly received both in Japan and internationally.

He made his major debut as a singer in April 2011 with the release of "Hana no Hana" under [[Tokuma Japan Communications]]. His third single, "Tokyo A Go Go," went on to reach No. 1 on the Wired Request Chart in the [[Enka]]/[[Kayōkyoku|Kayō]] category.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=花園直道オフィシャルモバイルサイトプロフィール |url=http://naomichi.net/sp/profile.html |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=花園直道オフィシャルサイト |language=ja-JP}}</ref>

He also performed internationally in countries like the United States, France, Taiwan, South Korea, and Thailand.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=ข่าวสด |date=2022-12-10 |title=นาโอมิจิ ฮานาโซโนะ จับมือ เรียวมะ ควอเทท นำความเป็นที่สุดด้านวัฒนธรรมญี่ปุ่น |url=https://www.khaosod.co.th/entertainment/news_7407975 |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=ข่าวสด |language=th}}</ref>

== Trivia ==

* His [[blood type]] is O.<ref name=":1" />
* His hobby is fishing.<ref name=":1" />
* His nickname is "'''Nao-chan''' (なおちゃん)."

{{Nihongo|'''Hiroyasu Tanaka'''|田中博康||}} is a retired Japanese [[jockey]] and current [[Horse trainer|racehorse trainer]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=田中博康師支える騎手時代の経験 - スポニチ Sponichi Annex ギャンブル |url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/gamble/news/2021/11/12/kiji/20211111s00004000686000c.html |access-date=2026-01-22 |website=スポニチ Sponichi Annex |language=ja|date=2021-11-12}}</ref>

== Career ==
{{Expand section|date=January 2026}}
In 2024, he became the trainer with the highest winning percentage in the JRA Awards with a winning percentage of 0.239, and also won the JRA Award for Outstanding Technical Trainer for the first time, which is determined by winning percentage, number of wins per stable, prize money earned, and number of races started.<ref>{{Cite web |title=「2024年度JRA賞」調教師・騎手部門の受賞者決定 優秀技術調教師は田中博康調教師、MVJは戸崎圭太騎手｜競馬実況web｜競馬｜ラジオNIKKEI |url=https://www.radionikkei.jp/keiba_article/news/2024jramvj.html |access-date=2026-01-22 |website=ラジオNIKKEI |language=ja}}</ref>

== Major wins as a jockey ==

* Queen Spumante (2009 [[Queen Elizabeth II Cup (Japan)|Queen Elizabeth II Cup]])<ref name=":0" />

== Major wins as a trainer ==

'''Franco Velarde''' (born 4 November 1994) is a [[Chileans|Chilean]] [[rugby union]] player. He represents {{nrut|Chile}} internationally, and for [[Selknam (rugby union)|Selknam]] in the [[Super Rugby Americas]] competition. He competed for Chile in the [[2023 Rugby World Cup]].

== Career ==
Velarde played for the Viña Rugby Club (formerly Viña Rugby Old Boys and Girls).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Los Cóndores en el Mundial de Francia 2023 |url=https://chile.rugby/?p=10399 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Chile Rugby |language=es}}</ref>

In 2017, he made his international debut for {{nrut|Chile}} against {{nrut|Brazil}}.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2021-10-21 |title=Chilean Franco Velarde on his way to Spain from Selknam |url=https://www.americasrugbynews.com/2021/10/21/chilean-franco-velarde-on-his-way-to-spain-from-selknam/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Americas Rugby News |language=en-US}}</ref> He played for Barça Rugby from 2017 to 2020 and scored 26 tries for the side.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2021-12-14 |title=Franco Velarde, nueva incorporación de SilverStorm El Salvador |url=https://www.rugbyelsalvador.com/franco-velarde-nueva-incorporacion-de-silverstorm-el-salvador/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Club de Rugby El Salvador |language=es}}</ref>

At the beginning of 2021, he returned to Chile and joined [[Selknam (rugby union)|Selknam]] in the [[Super Rugby Americas]] competition.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Later in October, he participated in {{nrut|Chile}}'s historic win against {{nrut|Canada}} in their bid to qualify for the World Cup.<ref name=":1" /> In late October, he signed with Spanish club, [[CR El Salvador|SilverStorm El Salvador]], who were leading the [[División de Honor de Rugby]] league.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

He was selected in {{nrut|Chile}}'s squad to the [[2023 Rugby World Cup]] in [[France]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-31 |title=Rugby World Cup Pool D squads: Leitch and Horie set for fourth tournament {{!}} World Rugby |url=https://www.world.rugby/news/830578/rugby-world-cup-pool-d-squads |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=www.world.rugby}}</ref>

In 2026, he signed with Ordizia Rugby Elkartea for a season.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2026-01-27 |title=Franco Velarde regresa a Europa con fichaje en el Ordizia Rugby de la División de Honor Española |url=https://www.rugbychile.cl/2026/01/27/franco-velarde-regresa-a-europa-con-fichaje-en-el-ordizia-rugby-de-la-division-de-honor-espanola/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Rugby Chile |language=es}}</ref> He previously had stints with French club, [[Stade Français]], and [[Castilla y León Iberians]] in Spain.<ref name=":3" />

{{short description|American rabbi and historian (born 1985)}}
{{distinguish|Zev Leff}}
'''Zev Eleff''' (born 1985) is an American rabbi, historian, and academic administrator specializing in Jewish studies and American religion. He is the twelfth president of [[Gratz College]], a private Jewish institution in [[Jenkintown, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="gratzbio">{{cite web |title=Office of the President |url=https://www.gratz.edu/about/leadership/office-of-the-president |publisher=Gratz College |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref> His scholarship focuses on American Judaism.

== Biography ==

Eleff was born in [[Philadelphia]] in 1985 and raised in [[Baltimore]] and [[Chicago]]. He received a Bachelor of Arts from [[Yeshiva University|Yeshiva College]] in 2009 and rabbinic ordination from the [[Rabbi Isaac Elchanan Theological Seminary]] in 2011. He earned a Master of Arts from [[Teachers College, Columbia University]] (2011), and a Ph.D. in Near Eastern and Judaic Studies from [[Brandeis University]] in 2015.<ref name="gratzbio" />

In 2021, Eleff was appointed the twelfth president of Gratz College.<ref name="gratzbio" /> Prior to his appointment at Gratz College, Eleff held senior academic administrative roles in Chicago. He served as chief academic officer of [[Hebrew Theological College]] and as vice provost of [[Touro College]] Illinois. He was among the youngest faculty members at Touro to be promoted to the rank of full professor.<ref name="gratzbio" />

His appointment to Gratz College was noted in regional Jewish media as part of a broader transition from academic leadership roles in Chicago, highlighting his work as a historian of American Judaism and his administrative experience.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zev Eleff moves from Charm City to Gratz College |url=https://www.jewishtimes.com/zev-eleff-moves-from-charm-city-to-gratz-college/ |publisher=Baltimore Jewish Times |date=2021-06-30 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref>

== Presidency of Gratz College ==

Eleff became president of Gratz College in 2021 during a period of institutional transition.<ref name="gratzbio" /> During this time, the college expanded its academic programs and physical footprint.

Gratz introduced new graduate programs in antisemitism studies, including a master’s degree described in reporting as among the first of its kind in the United States.<ref>{{cite news |last=Saffren |first=Jarrad |title=Gratz College Debuting New Master's Program in Antisemitism Studies |url=https://www.jewishexponent.com/gratz-college-debuting-new-masters-program-in-antisemitism-studies/ |publisher=Jewish Exponent |date=2024-02-14 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Gratz College launches 'first-of-its-kind' master's degree on antisemitism |url=https://ejewishphilanthropy.com/gratz-college-launches-first-of-its-kind-masters-degree-on-antisemitism/ |publisher=eJewishPhilanthropy |date=2024-02-20 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref> A doctoral program in antisemitism studies followed, developed in response to growing demand for expertise in the field.<ref>{{cite news |last=Snyder |first=Susan |title=Gratz College offers doctoral degree in antisemitism studies |url=https://www.inquirer.com/education/gratz-college-antisemitism-studies-degree-20250804.html |publisher=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=2025-08-04 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref>

The college also expanded doctoral education in Jewish studies through an Executive Ph.D. program designed for working professionals, along with fellowship initiatives such as the Walder Fellowship, which supports Orthodox Jewish women pursuing advanced study.<ref>{{cite web |title=Executive PhD in Jewish Studies |url=https://www.gratz.edu/academics/program/jewish-studies/executive-phd-jewish-studies |publisher=Gratz College |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Gratz College names inaugural Walder Fellowship cohort for its Executive PhD in Jewish Studies |url=https://jewishlink.news/gratz-college-names-inaugural-walder-fellowship-cohort-for-its-executive-phd-in-jewish-studies/ |publisher=Jewish Link |date=2025-06-05 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref>

Additional initiatives included expansion of faculty leadership in [[Holocaust studies|Holocaust]] and [[antisemitism]] studies, including the appointment of Ayal Feinberg as director of the Center for Holocaust Studies and Human Rights.<ref>{{cite news |title=You Should Know… Ayal Feinberg, Gratz’s new director of Holocaust studies |url=https://www.jewishexponent.com/you-should-know-ayal-feinberg-gratzs-new-director-of-holocaust-studies/ |publisher=Jewish Exponent |date=2023-11-01 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref>

Gratz also developed digital scholarship initiatives, including the Grayzel Digital Platform and a digital archive project in partnership with the Elie Wiesel Foundation for Humanity.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gratz College Launches Grayzel Digital Platform |url=https://www.gratz.edu/news-and-events/event-calendar/default-dynamic-news-page/~board/news-and-events/post/gratz-college-launches-grayzel-digital-platform |publisher=Gratz College |date=2025-11-06 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Gratz College Digitizing Elie Wiesel Collection |url=https://www.jewishexponent.com/gratz-college-digitizing-elie-wiesel-collection/ |publisher=Jewish Exponent |date=2024-04-22 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref>

The college also undertook a physical expansion to Philadelphia’s [[Philadelphia Main Line|Main Line]], including redevelopment of properties in [[Bala Cynwyd]] as part of a long-term campus plan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gratz College Breaks Ground on Bala Cynwyd Property |url=https://www.mainlinemedianews.com/2025/11/02/gratz-college-breaks-ground-on-bala-cynwyd-property/ |publisher=Main Line Media News |date=2025-11-02 |access-date=2026-05-01}}</ref>

== Scholarship ==

Eleff is a historian of American Judaism whose work examines the development of Jewish religious life in the United States. His research has addressed topics including [[Orthodox Judaism]], religion and sports, and aspects of American cultural history.

== Selected works ==

* ''Living from Convention to Convention: A History of the NCSY, 1954–1980'' (2009)
* ''Who Rules the Synagogue?: Religious Authority and the Formation of American Judaism'' (2016)
* ''Modern Orthodox Judaism: A Documentary History'' (2016)
* ''A Century at the Center: Orthodox Judaism and the Jewish Center'' (2018)
* ''Authentically Orthodox: A Tradition-Bound Faith in American Life'' (2020)
* ''Dyed in Crimson: Football, Faith, and Remaking Harvard's America'' (2023)
* ''The Greatest of All Time: A History of an American Obsession'' (2025)

== Reception ==

Eleff’s scholarship has been reviewed in academic journals. Writing in ''American Jewish History'', [[David Ellenson]] described ''Modern Orthodox Judaism: A Documentary History'' as “a superb volume.”<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ellenson |first=David |title=Modern Orthodox Judaism: A Documentary History (review) |journal=American Jewish History |volume=101 |issue=3 |year=2017 |pages=401–404}}</ref> A review in ''The Review of Rabbinic Judaism'' characterized the work as “invaluable for its primary source extracts” and praised its “scope and fairness.”<ref>{{cite journal |title=Modern Orthodox Judaism: A Documentary History (review) |journal=The Review of Rabbinic Judaism |year=2017}}</ref>

In ''Religious Studies Review'', Edward S. Shapiro described ''Who Rules the Synagogue?'' as a “major contribution” to the historiography of American Judaism.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Shapiro |first=Edward S. |title=Who Rules the Synagogue? (review) |journal=Religious Studies Review |year=2017}}</ref>

Reviews of ''Authentically Orthodox'' have emphasized both its analytical framework and narrative qualities. Yaakov Bieler noted its engagement with major debates in American Orthodoxy,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Bieler |first=Yaakov |title=Authentically Orthodox (review) |journal=Tradition |volume=53 |issue=1 |year=2021}}</ref> while Asher Oser wrote that “Eleff is a master storyteller.”<ref>{{cite journal |last=Oser |first=Asher |title=Authentically Orthodox (review) |journal=The American Jewish Archives Journal |year=2021}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

Eleff has received awards including the Wasserman Prize of the American Jewish Historical Society and a Rockower Award for Excellence from the American Jewish Press Association.<ref name="gratzbio" /> His books have twice been named finalists for the National Jewish Book Award.<ref name="gratzbio" />

In 2024, he was named a “Trailblazer in Higher Education” by ''City & State Pennsylvania''.<ref name="gratzbio" />

== Personal life ==

Eleff resides in Merion Station, Pennsylvania, with his wife and their children.<ref name="gratzbio" />

'''Nanase Shoji''' {{Nihongo|2=庄司 七瀬|4=born 1989}} is a Japanese retired individual [[Rhythmic gymnastics|rhythmic gymnast]]. She now works for Yamagata City Hall.<ref name="ynp1109">{{Cite web |date=2011-09-08 |title=地元出身トップアスリート３人が市職員に　故郷山形での活躍期待 |trans-title=3 Local Top Athletes Become City Employees - High Hopes in Their Native Yamagata |url=https://www.yamagata-np.jp/news/201109/08/kj_2011090801318.php |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2012-0417-0107-05/yamagata-np.jp/news/201109/08/kj_2011090801318.php |archive-date=2012-04-17 |website=Yamagata News Online |language=Japanese}}</ref>

== Career ==
Shoji was born in [[Yamagata Prefecture]] and began training in rhythmic gymnastics there when she was five years old.<ref name="ns0706">{{Cite web |last=塩谷 |first=正人 |date=2007-06-02 |title=31年ぶり３年連続女王へ |trans-title=For the First Time in 31 Years, a 3-time Queen |url=http://tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/p-tn-tp2-20070602-207575.html |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2012-0417-0129-36/tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/p-tn-tp2-20070602-207575.html |archive-date=2012-04-17 |website=nikkansports.com |language=Japanese}}</ref> As a gymnast, she was known for her pivots (spins)<ref name="ys0605">{{Cite web |last=椎名 |first=桂子 |date=2006-05-23 |title=“努力の人”高橋の優勝　新体操新時代の足音 |trans-title="Hard worker" Takahashi Wins - A New Era of Rhythmic Gymnastics is Approaching |url=http://sportsnavi.yahoo.co.jp/other/column/200605/at00009179.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060915015712/http://sportsnavi.yahoo.co.jp/other/column/200605/at00009179.html |archive-date=2006-09-15 |website=sportsnavi.com |language=Japanese}}</ref> as well as her speed and power.<ref name="ns0608">{{Cite web |last=高宮 |first=憲治 |date=2006-08-08 |title=山形北・庄司が連覇 |trans-title=North Yamagata's Shouji Wins Again |url=http://tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/p-tn-tp2-20060808-72509.html |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2012-0417-0128-19/tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/p-tn-tp2-20060808-72509.html |archive-date=2012-04-17 |website=nikkansports.com |language=Japanese}}</ref>

In 2004, she came in second at the Japanese National Middle School Women's Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-08-21 |title=第35回全国中学校新体操選手権大会 |trans-title=35th National Middle School Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2004/result/pdf/04zcr_i.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050228213544/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2004/result/pdf/04zcr_i.pdf |archive-date=2005-02-28 |website=Japanese Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> In August 2005, she won her first of three National High School Athletic Championships titles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2005-08-13 |title=大西完全制覇－インターハイ |trans-title=Onishi Completely Dominates - Inter-High School Championships |url=https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/sports/local/20050813000106 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127153034/https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/sports/local/20050813000106 |archive-date=2024-11-27 |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=ShikokuNews |language=Japanese}}</ref> In September, she competed at the [[2005–2006 FIG Rhythmic Gymnastics World Cup series|World Cup]] stage in [[Varna, Bulgaria]], where she placed 5th.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2005-09-04 |title=2005 バルナ国際競技会 |trans-title=2005 Varna World Cup |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2005/result/pdf/05bul_s.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425015639/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2005/result/pdf/05bul_s.pdf |archive-date=2012-04-25 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> That November, she was fourth at the [[Japanese Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships|Japanese Championships]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kobayashi |first=Takako |date=2005-11-07 |title=Rhythmic Gymnastics Japanese Nationals 2005 |url=https://www.gymmedia.com/rhythmic-gymnastics/Rhythmic-Gymnastics-Japanese-Nationals-2005 |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=Gymmedia.com}}</ref>

The next year, in May, she competed at the Japanese Youth Championships. She demonstrated her skill with pivots at the competition and won the silver medal, but she said that "I couldn't perform acceptably". She competed at the [[2005–2006 FIG Rhythmic Gymnastics World Cup series|World Cup]] stage in [[Irkutsk]] in June and finished in 16th place.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-06-24 |title=2006イルクーツク国際 |trans-title=Irkutst World Cup |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2006/result/pdf/06ilk.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425024205/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2006/result/pdf/06ilk.pdf |archive-date=2012-04-25 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> In August, she won her second National High School Athletic Championships; she was the first rhythmic gymnast to repeat her victory there since [[Rieko Matsunaga]] had done so 9 years earlier.<ref name="ns0608" />

In March 2007, Shoji won the National High School Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships in March. In May, she competed in a selection competition for international competitions, but after making mistakes in her clubs and ribbon routines, she finished in 13th place.<ref name="jg0705">{{Cite web |date=2007-05-06 |title=第28回世界新体操選手権大会日本代表決定競技会 |trans-title=The 28th World Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships Representative Selection Competition |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2007/result/pdf/07wchftr.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425035705/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2007/result/pdf/07wchftr.pdf |archive-date=2012-04-25 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> Later in May, she placed fourth at the Japanese Youth Championships.<ref name="ns0706" /> In August, she won her third consecutive National High School Athletic Championships. She was the second-ever women's rhythmic gymnast to do so after Kumiko Fumoto did so 31 years before her. Shoji said that she had won her third consecutive title "by chance" and that she had wanted to compete without making mistakes, since it was her last Championships.<ref name="ns0708">{{Cite web |date=2007-08-04 |title=庄司３連覇も「たまたまです」／高校総体 |trans-title=Shoji's Third Consecutive Victory "By chance" |url=http://tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/f-tn-tp2-20070804-236957.html |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2012-0417-0126-17/tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/f-tn-tp2-20070804-236957.html |archive-date=2012-04-17 |website=Nikkansports.com |language=Japanese}}</ref> In November, she placed 9th at the Japanese Championships. Afterward, she expressed hope that she would be selected for the [[2009 World Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships|2009 World Championships]], held in [[Mie, Japan]], and stated that she had chosen to attend the Tokyo Women's College of Physical Education, where many Olympic rhythmic gymnasts have studied.<ref>{{Cite web |last=柴田 |first=寛人 |date=2007-12-13 |title=新体操の庄司が東女体大進学 |trans-title=Rhythmic Gymnast Shoji to Attend Tokyo Women's College of Physical Education |url=http://tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/p-tn-tp2-20071213-294990.html |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2012-0417-0127-19/tohoku.nikkansports.com/news/p-tn-tp2-20071213-294990.html |archive-date=2012-04-17 |website=Nikkansports.com |language=Japanese}}</ref>

In September 2008, she competed in the National Collegiate Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships and finished in second place.<ref name="jg0809">{{Cite web |date=2008-09-06 |title=第60回 全日本学生新体操選手権大会 |trans-title=60th National Collegiate Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2008/result/pdf/08icr_wi.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120627150850/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2008/result/pdf/08icr_wi.pdf |archive-date=2012-06-27 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> She placed 5th at the National Championships in December.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-12-06 |title=第61回 全日本新体操選手権大会 |trans-title=61st Japanese Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2008/result/pdf/08nar_wi.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120530123915/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2008/result/pdf/08nar_wi.pdf |archive-date=2012-05-30 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref>

The next year, she was selected for the [[2009 World Games]] held in Taiwan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-05-06 |title=日高が首位で最終選考会へ／世界新体操の２次選考会 |trans-title=Hidaka Advances to Final Selection Round in First Place / World Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships 2nd Selection Round |url=https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/sports/international/20090506000251 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223065522/http://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/sports/international/20090506000251 |archive-date=2025-02-23 |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=Shikoku News |language=Japanese}}</ref> She competed there in July; her best result was 16th place in the hoop competition.<ref name="jg09012">{{Cite web |title=１、平成 21 年度 事業報告 |trans-title=2009 Program Report |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/association/report/2009/pdf/rep09.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120816015748/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/association/report/2009/pdf/rep09.pdf |archive-date=2012-08-16 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> In August, she won a second silver all-around medal at the National Collegiate Championships, and she won the ribbon final.<ref name="jg0908">{{Cite web |date=2009-08-16 |title=第61回 全日本学生新体操選手権大会 |trans-title=61st National Collegiate Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2009/result/pdf/09icr_wi.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425025801/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2009/result/pdf/09icr_wi.pdf |archive-date=2012-04-25 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-08-17 |title=第61回 全日本学生新体操選手権大会 |trans-title=61st National Collegiate Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2009/result/pdf/09icr_ef.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425025805/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2009/result/pdf/09icr_ef.pdf |archive-date=2012-04-25 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> In October, she participated in the [[2009 Asian Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships|Asian Championships]], where she competed with rope (5th place) and ribbon (7th place).<ref name="jg09012" />

Shoji continued to competed in 2010, but it was a difficult year for her, and she made an unusual number of mistakes in competition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=椎名 |first=桂子 |date=2010-11-17 |title=オールジャパン直前企画27　大学生以上の女子選手たち⑤　 |trans-title=All-Japan Pre-Competition Feature #27: Female Athletes (University Level and Above) — Part 5 |url=http://www.plus-blog.sportsnavi.com/rg-lovers/article/357 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730172456/http://www.plus-blog.sportsnavi.com/rg-lovers/article/357 |archive-date=2017-07-30 |website=Sportsnavi |language=Japanese}}</ref>

The Tokyo Women's College of Physical Education Rhythmic Gymnastics Club attends a training camp in [[Yamagata Prefecture]] every year. However, in 2011, the camp was almost cancelled due to the [[aftermath of the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami]]. The Yamagata Rhythmic Gymnastics Association requested that the training camp be held once the gymnasium, which had been in use as an evacuation center, became available again. The club held a free showcase during the camp. Shoji was one of the members who attended. Along with her fellow Yamagata native teammate [[Nachi Misawa]], she stated ahead of the showcase, "We're hearing that many people from [[Tōhoku region|Tōhoku]] will come to watch, so we want to extend cheer to the victims through our performances."<ref name="yn1108">{{Cite web |date=2011-08-26 |title=東女体大新体操部が合宿開始　山形・三沢ら県勢3人参加 |trans-title=Tokyo Women's College of Physical Education Rhythmic Gymnastics Club Begins Training Camp - Three Local Athletes Including Yamagata and Misawa Participate |url=http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201108/26/kj_2011082600893.php |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2012-0417-0156-47/yamagata-np.jp/news/201108/26/kj_2011082600893.php |archive-date=2012-04-17 |website=Yamagata News Online |language=Japanese}}</ref>

In August 2011, she finished 10th at her final National Collegiate Championships.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-08-05 |title=第63回 全日本学生新体操選手権大会 |trans-title=63rd National Collegiate Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships |url=http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2011/result/pdf/11icr_wi.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120627100736/http://www.jpn-gym.or.jp/rhythmic/2011/result/pdf/11icr_wi.pdf |archive-date=2012-06-27 |website=Japan Gymnastics Association |language=Japanese}}</ref> The following month, she was accepted as a [[Yamagata (city)|Yamagata]] city employee through a special selection process. She said of her new position, "Until now, I was in the position of being supported by Yamagata. I want to repay that."<ref>{{Cite news |last=安藤 |first=龍朗 |last2=浅妻 |first2=博之 |last3=鈴木 |first3=健太 |date=2012-04-03 |title=入社・辞令交付式 各地で 新社会人、決意新た |trans-title=New Employee and Appointment Change Ceremonies: Everywhere, New Working Adults Have Renewed Resolve |work=[[Mainichi Shimbun]] |language=Japanese}}</ref>

'''Sara Alonso Martínez''' (born 1999) is a Spanish long-distance runner who specialises in [[trail running]] and [[mountain running]]. A former [[3000 metres steeplechase|3,000 metres steeplechase]] athlete, she became Spanish trail running champion in 2022 and the same year won both the [[Transgrancanaria]] Marathon and the [[Marathon du Mont Blanc]], briefly leading the [[Golden Trail Series|Golden Trail World Series]] standings; in 2025 she won the [[Zegama-Aizkorri]] mountain marathon, took silver at the [[2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships]] in [[Canfranc]] and finished as runner-up in the Golden Trail World Series.<ref>{{cite web |last=de Torres |first=Carlos |title=Sara Alonso y el equipo femenino lograron sendas platas en el Mundial de montaña y trail running |trans-title=Sara Alonso and the women's team won silver medals at the Mountain and Trail Running World Championships |url=https://www.visibilitas.com/atletismo-mundial-montana-trail-running-sara-alonso-equipo-femenino-plata/ |website=Visibilitas |language=es |date=27 September 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>

While studying a double degree in physiotherapy and Physical Activity and Sport Sciences at the [[University of Lleida]], she made the transition to mountain running through a class trip to the [[Pyrenees]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso: "Clasificarme para el Europeo sería brutal" |trans-title=Sara Alonso: "Qualifying for the European Championships would be brutal" |url=https://www.donostitik.com/sara-alonso-clasificarme-para-el-europeo-seria-brutal/ |website=Donostitik |language=es |date=23 April 2021 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> She joined the [[Salomon Group|Salomon]] España trail team in 2019 after contacting them via [[Instagram]], and made her debut on the [[Golden Trail Series|Golden Trail World Series]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last=Soriano |first=Luis Miguel López |title=Sara Alonso, del tartán a la conquista de la montaña en 'Go Sara' |trans-title=Sara Alonso, from the track to conquering the mountain in 'Go Sara' |url=https://carreraspormontana.com/carreras/sara-alonso-del-tartan-a-la-conquista-de-la-montana-en-go-sara/ |website=Carreraspormontana.com |language=es |date=24 May 2022 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> A full-time professional athlete, she has reported training around 130 to 140 kilometres a week in the build-up to her main races.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cuántos kilómetros corre antes de Zegama Sara Alonso |trans-title=How many kilometres Sara Alonso runs before Zegama |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/outdoor/cuantos-kilometros-corre-antes-zegama-sara-alonso-117324461 |website=Sport |language=es |date=22 May 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> Winning the [[Zegama-Aizkorri]] mountain marathon, on home soil in the Basque Country, has been described as a long-standing personal goal of hers.<ref>{{cite web |title="Quería hacerle ficha al ganar Zegama-Aizkorri": la historia de lucha de Sara Alonso |trans-title="I wanted to put my name on the Zegama-Aizkorri trophy": the story of Sara Alonso's struggle |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/running/20250527/1002472893/querer-hacerle-ficha-ganar-zegama-aizkorri-historia-lucha-sara-alonso.html |website=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |date=27 May 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>
 
== Career ==
 
=== 2022: Breakthrough season ===
 
Alonso opened 2022 by winning the marathon distance of the [[Transgrancanaria]] in 3:30:10, taking her first major international title ahead of South Africa's Toni McCann and Spain's Anna Comet.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sánchez Santamaría |first=Teresa |title=Sara Alonso se lleva la victoria en la maratón de Transgrancanaria |trans-title=Sara Alonso takes victory in the Transgrancanaria marathon |url=https://www.trailrun.es/cronicas/sara-alonso-se-lleva-victoria-en-maraton-transgrancanaria_252403_102.html |website=TrailRun |language=es |date=5 March 2022 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> A few months later she earned a podium finish at the Zegama-Aizkorri mountain marathon, and on 4 June 2022 she was crowned Spanish trail running champion at Riópar ([[Albacete]]), leading a sweep for [[Bilbao Atletismo]] alongside teammates Onditz Iturbe and Yolanda Martín.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alejandro García y Sara Alonso, nuevos campeones de Carreras de Montaña |trans-title=Alejandro García and Sara Alonso, new mountain running champions |url=https://www.carreraspopulares.com/noticia/alejandro-garcia-y-sara-alonso-nuevos-campeones-de-carreras-de-montana |website=Carreraspopulares.com |language=es |date=4 June 2022 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> A week later she won the Olla Vertical de Núria, a 3.78 km vertical race with 949 metres of positive elevation rising from the Sanctuary of Núria to the summit of [[Puigmal]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sánchez Santamaría |first=Teresa |title=Sara Alonso y Albert Pérez vencedores de l'Olla Vertical |trans-title=Sara Alonso and Albert Pérez, winners of l'Olla Vertical |url=https://www.trailrun.es/cronicas/sara-alonso-albert-perez-vencedores-olla-vertical-2022_258494_102.html |website=TrailRun |language=es |date=11 June 2022 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>
 
On 26 June 2022 Alonso won the [[Marathon du Mont Blanc]], a 42-kilometre race finishing in the centre of [[Chamonix]], in 4:14:49, more than five minutes ahead of New Zealand's Caitlin Fielder. The result gave her her first Golden Trail World Series victory and the provisional lead of the circuit.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso gana el Marathon du Mont-Blanc 2022 y se pone líder de las Golden |trans-title=Sara Alonso wins the 2022 Marathon du Mont-Blanc and takes the Golden Trail Series lead |url=https://carreraspormontana.com/carreras/sara-alonso-gana-el-marathon-du-mont-blanc-2022-y-se-pone-lider-de-las-golden/ |website=Carreraspormontana.com |language=es |date=26 June 2022 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> She finished the season third in the Golden Trail World Series overall standings. At the end of 2022 she announced the end of her partnership with Salomon España and subsequently signed with [[Asics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso defenderá su título en la Transgrancanaria SWE Maratón |trans-title=Sara Alonso will defend her title at the Transgrancanaria SWE Marathon |url=https://www.canarias7.es/deportes/mas-deportes/sara-alonso-defendera-20221215181850-nt.html |website=Canarias7 |language=es |date=15 December 2022 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>
 
=== 2025: Zegama win, Canfranc silver and Golden Trail runner-up ===
 
After missing the 2023 season with a stress fracture and the 2024 Zegama marathon due to pneumonia,<ref name="elconfidencial">{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso, la corredora vasca que ha ganado la Zegama-Aizkorri |trans-title=Sara Alonso, the Basque runner who has won the Zegama-Aizkorri |url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/otros-deportes/2025-05-25/sara-alonso-corredora-vasca-zegama-aizkorri-1qrt_4136857/ |website=El Confidencial |language=es |date=25 May 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> Alonso opened the 2025 [[Golden Trail Series|Golden Trail World Series]] season with victory in the Kobe Trail in [[Kobe]], Japan, on 19 April, finishing in 2:53:57 ahead of Romania's Madalina Florea and Spain's Malen Osa.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alonso and Kipngeno take the win in Kobe at the opening round of the 2025 Golden Trail World Series |url=https://goldentrailseries.com/alonso-and-kipngeno-take-the-win-in-kobe-at-the-opening-round-of-the-2025-golden-trail-world-series/ |website=Golden Trail World Series |language=en |date=19 April 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> Her return to Zegama after two consecutive missed editions was widely covered in the Spanish press,<ref>{{cite web |last=Larrea |first=Iker |title=La odisea de Sara Alonso y Malen Osa por ser profetas en la maratón de montaña de Zegama |trans-title=The odyssey of Sara Alonso and Malen Osa to be prophets in the Zegama mountain marathon |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2025-05-24/la-odisea-de-sara-alonso-y-malen-osa-por-ser-profetas-en-la-maraton-de-montana-de-zegama.html |website=El País |language=es |date=24 May 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> and on 25 May 2025 she led the race from start to finish to win her home mountain marathon in 4:27:25, ahead of Switzerland's Judith Wyder and her compatriot Malen Osa.<ref name="elconfidencial" />
 
In July 2025, while training in the Pyrenees, Alonso was charged from behind by a cow and sustained a fractured sixth rib, forcing her to withdraw from [[Sierre-Zinal]] and the [[Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc#OCC|OCC]] race of the [[Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso se perderá Sierre-Zinal y UTMB tras ser embestida por una vaca |trans-title=Sara Alonso to miss Sierre-Zinal and UTMB after being charged by a cow |url=https://maratonradio.com/noticias/sara-alonso-trail-running-lesion-vaca/ |website=Maratón Radio |language=es |date=16 July 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso, atleta: "Me ha atacado una vaca, me ha roto una costilla y pensé que iba a morir" |trans-title=Sara Alonso, athlete: "I was attacked by a cow, it broke one of my ribs and I thought I was going to die" |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/television/20250714/10888756/sara-alonso-atleta-me-atacado-vaca-me-roto-costilla-pense-iba-morir-gvm2.html |website=La Vanguardia |language=es |date=14 July 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso, atleta embestida por una vaca |trans-title=Sara Alonso, the athlete charged by a cow |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2025/07/15/sara-alonso-atleta-embestida-vacachatgpt-dice-probabilidad-05-ahi-/00031752575410828146916.htm |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es |date=15 July 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>
 
She returned later in the summer, finishing fifth in the OCC at UTMB, before competing at the [[2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships]] in [[Canfranc]], where, on 26 September, she took the silver medal in the short trail (44.4-kilometre) race in 5:38:15, behind [[Tove Alexandersson]] and ahead of Britain's Naomi Lang by 39 seconds; the Spanish team also won silver behind Sweden.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tranchand and Alexandersson shatter short trail records at Canfranc |url=https://worldathletics.org/news/report/world-mountain-trail-running-championships-canfrancpirineos-2025 |website=World Athletics |language=en |date=26 September 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Mock |first=Justin |title=2025 Trail World Championships Short Trail Results: Tove Alexandersson, Frédéric Tranchand Triumph |url=https://www.irunfar.com/2025-trail-world-championships-short-trail-results |website=iRunFar |language=en |date=27 September 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso, subcampeona mundial en Canfranc |trans-title=Sara Alonso, world runner-up in Canfranc |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/outdoor/sara-alonso-subcampeona-mundial-canfranc-121991096 |website=Sport |language=es |date=26 September 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> On 11 October she finished third at the Ledro Sky Trentino Grand Finale, the closing event of the 2025 Golden Trail World Series, sealing the runner-up position in the overall standings (913 points), behind Madalina Florea (958) and ahead of Lauren Gregory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Plata para Sara Alonso en las Golden Trail World Series |trans-title=Silver for Sara Alonso in the Golden Trail World Series |url=https://www.diariovasco.com/mendira/plata-sara-alonso-golden-trail-world-series-20251011152324-nt.html |website=El Diario Vasco |language=es |date=11 October 2025 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>
 
=== 2026 season ===
 
Alonso opened her 2026 campaign in the [[Skyrunner World Series]]. In March she won Acantilados del Norte in [[La Palma]], the third round of the circuit, repeating Spain's double victory alongside [[Manuel Merillas]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Manuel Merillas y Sara Alonso brillan en una edición apasionante de Acantilados del Norte |trans-title=Manuel Merillas and Sara Alonso shine in an exciting edition of Acantilados del Norte |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/running/carreras/20260316/1004153437/manuel-merillas-sara-alonso-brillan-edicion-apasionante-acantilados-norte.html |website=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |date=16 March 2026 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> On 11 April 2026 she won the Calamorro Skyrace in [[Benalmádena]] in 3:25:42, taking her second consecutive World Series victory and the lead in the women's overall standings.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso y Manu Merillas brillan en una Calamorro Skyrace de altísimo nivel |trans-title=Sara Alonso and Manu Merillas shine in a top-level Calamorro Skyrace |url=https://www.msn.com/es-es/deportes/motor/sara-alonso-y-manu-merillas-brillan-en-una-calamorro-skyrace-de-altisimo-nivel/ar-AA20I4Hm |website=MSN |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |date=12 April 2026 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref> She subsequently turned her attention to the defence of her [[Zegama-Aizkorri]] title, scheduled for May 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sara Alonso encara la Zegama-Aizkorri |trans-title=Sara Alonso prepares for the Zegama-Aizkorri |url=https://www.diariovasco.com/mendira/sara-alonso-zegama-aizkorri-20260417065709-nt.html |website=El Diario Vasco |language=es |date=17 April 2026 |access-date=1 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Theo Montoya''' (born 1992) is a [[Colombia]]n filmmaker.

== Life and career ==
Montoya was born in 1992 in [[Medellín]], Colombia. Founder and director of ''DESVIO VISUAL'', a production company focused on experimental film and documentary work.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Tribeca Film Institute |url=https://www.tfiny.org/filmmakers/detail/theo_montoya#:~:text=Theo%20Montoya,%20born%20in%201992,of%20experimental%20films%20and%20documentaries. |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=www.tfiny.org}}</ref> ''Anhell69'' (2022), his debut feature film, an international co-production involving [[Colombia]], [[Romania]], [[France]], and [[Germany]], premiered at the [[79th Venice International Film Festival]], and won a Special Mention by the Grand Jury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Residents |url=https://cinemadedemain.festival-cannes.com/en/supporting/the-residents/ |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=Cinéma de Demain |language=en-US}}</ref>

For over seven years, Montoya has worked with youth-led audiovisual projects in [[Medellín]], with a focus on queer narratives, nihilism, and social realities. In 2018, he received the ''Colombian Cinematographic Development Fund'' for his short documentary ''Son of Sodom'', the short version of his first feature.<ref name=":0" /> In 2024, he participated at La Résidence of the [[Cannes Film Festival]]. Afterwards, he became part of the [[2026 Cannes Film Festival]] with his short ''Thunder Platoon'' is based on [[Colombia]]’s [["False positives" scandal|“false positives” scandal]], where civilians, often from marginalized groups, were killed by the army and falsely presented as terrorists. It follows soldiers celebrating such an attack.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-20 |title=Undercurrents of normality permeate this year's short films at Cannes |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/491664/ |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=[[Cineuropa]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''Victoria Sevilla Vázquez''' (born 28 March 1992), known professionally as '''Vicky Sevilla''', is a Spanish [[chef]]. Born in [[Quart de les Valls]], in the [[province of Valencia]], she came to cooking after taking a job at a beach bar in [[Formentera]] as a teenager, and afterwards trained at the hospitality school of [[Castellón de la Plana|Castellón]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Lakunza |first=Rosana |title=Vicky Sevilla: "Todo empezó para mí en un chiringuito de playa" |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla: "It all started for me in a beach bar" |url=https://www.deia.eus/on/2023/01/03/empezo-chiringuito-playa-6329477.html |website=Deia |language=es |date=3 January 2023 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In 2017 she opened Arrels in [[Sagunto]], in the former stables of a medieval palace, and has led it as owner and head chef since then.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vicky Sevilla, del restaurant Arrels de Sagunt, premiada com a "gran promesa" per l'Acadèmia Internacional de Gastronomia |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, of the Arrels restaurant in Sagunt, awarded as a "great promise" by the International Academy of Gastronomy |url=https://www.apuntmedia.es/noticies/societat/vicky-sevilla-restaurant-arrels-sagunt-premiada-gran-promesa-l-academia-internacional-gastronomia_1_1881031.html |website=À Punt |language=ca |date=1 July 2026 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> Arrels received a [[Michelin Guide|Michelin star]] in December 2021, when Sevilla was 29, making her the youngest woman in Spain to obtain the distinction.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vicky Sevilla recibe el premio New Talent of the Year de la Liste Mediterranean 2023 |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla receives the New Talent of the Year award from La Liste Mediterranean 2023 |url=https://valenciaplaza.com/guiahedonista/comer3/vicky-sevilla-recibe-el-premio-new-talent-of-the-year-de-la-liste-mediterranean-2023 |website=Valencia Plaza |language=es |date=24 March 2023 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> It has kept the star in later editions of the guide, including the 2026 selection.<ref>{{cite web |title=La Comunitat Valenciana brilla en la Guía Michelin 2026: mantiene todas sus Estrellas y suma tres nuevos restaurantes |trans-title=The Valencian Community shines in the 2026 Michelin Guide: it keeps all its Stars and adds three new restaurants |url=https://www.elperiodic.com/comunitat-valenciana-brilla-guia-michelin-2026-mantiene-todas-estrellas-suma-tres-nuevos-restaurantes_1047623 |website=elperiodic.com |language=es |date=26 November 2025 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The restaurant also holds one Sol from the [[Repsol Guide]], and Sevilla's other distinctions include the La Liste Mediterranean New Talent of the Year award and the Prix au Chef de l'Avenir.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vicky Sevilla recibe el Prix au Chef de l'Avenir de la academia internacional de gastronomía |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla receives the Prix au Chef de l'Avenir from the international academy of gastronomy |url=https://valenciaplaza.com/guiahedonista/comer3/vicky-sevilla-recibe-el-prix-au-chef-de-lavenir-de-la-academia-internacional-de-gastronomia |website=Valencia Plaza |language=es |date=3 July 2026 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and training ==

Sevilla has said that she came to cooking by chance. At 17, going through a difficult period, she travelled to Formentera to visit a friend and had to find work there; she took a job in a kitchen without knowing how to fry an egg, was running the cold station four months later, and has said that "cooking saved me". She then trained at the hospitality school of Castellón.<ref>{{cite web |last=García |first=Amaya |title=Vicky Sevilla, la chef más joven en lograr la estrella Michelin: "La cocina me salvó" |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, the youngest chef to obtain the Michelin star: "Cooking saved me" |url=https://www.elmundo.es/metropoli/gastronomia/2021/12/15/61b9bd4221efa0964a8b456f.html |website=El Mundo |language=es |date=15 December 2021 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The accommodation she had been promised on the island did not materialise and she slept on a bed improvised from pallets; she stayed for two seasons in a kitchen she has described as harsh, on one occasion being made to clean a freezer at −40 °C as a punishment, and later opened her own restaurant with a state-backed ICO loan and, as she has stressed, without partners or investors.<ref>{{cite web |last=Nadal |first=Irene |title=Vicky Sevilla, de dormir en palés a ser la mujer más joven con una estrella Michelin: menú a 75 € |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, from sleeping on pallets to being the youngest woman with a Michelin star: €75 menu |url=https://www.elespanol.com/reportajes/20230408/vicky-sevilla-dormir-pales-estrella-michelin-eur/754174642_0.html |website=El Español |language=es |date=8 April 2023 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The Formentera restaurant served some 300 covers per service, in contrast with the 25 places of her own dining room.<ref>{{cite web |title=Así es Arrels (Sagunto), el restaurante de Vicky Sevilla, la chef con estrella Michelin más joven de España |trans-title=This is Arrels (Sagunto), the restaurant of Vicky Sevilla, the youngest Michelin-starred chef in Spain |url=https://www.directoalpaladar.com/viajes/vicky-sevilla-arrels-estrella-michelin-joven-espana-mi-obsesion-era-tener-gastronomico-rentable |website=Directo al Paladar |language=es |date=19 April 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

Back on the mainland she cooked under three Valencian chefs whom she has repeatedly credited: Susi Díaz, at La Finca in [[Elche]], from whom she says she learned the value of doing things properly; [[Begoña Rodrigo]], at La Salita in Valencia, whom she describes as a mirror to look into; and Vicente Patiño, at Saiti in Valencia, with whom she learned everything from management to pastry.<ref>{{cite web |last=López |first=Silvia |title=Hablamos con la chef Vicky Sevilla: "Temí que la estrella Michelin me vaciara el restaurante, que la gente pensara que Arrels tenía que ser muy caro" |trans-title=We talk to chef Vicky Sevilla: "I feared the Michelin star would empty my restaurant, that people would think Arrels had to be very expensive" |url=https://www.mujerhoy.com/actualidad/hablamos-chef-vicky-sevilla-estrella-michelin-restaurante-arrels-20220115131629-nt.html |website=Mujer Hoy |language=es |date=15 January 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The gastronomy magazine ''7 Caníbales'' has described Patiño in particular as her master.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vicky Sevilla, la fuerza de las raíces |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, the strength of the roots |url=https://www.7canibales.com/opinion/vicky-sevilla/ |website=7 Caníbales |language=es |date=4 January 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Arrels ===

Sevilla opened Arrels on 12 October 2017, at the age of 25. The restaurant serves a tasting menu that changes with the season, so that diners do not know in advance what they will be eating; she has said that she works with humble, local and seasonal products and reinterprets traditional recipes with a good deal of freedom.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sánchez |first=Clara Román |title=Vicky Sevilla, de Arrels, la chef más joven de España con estrella Michelin |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, of Arrels, the youngest chef in Spain with a Michelin star |url=https://restauracionnews.com/2022/01/vicky-sevilla-chef-de-arrels-y-la-mujer-mas-joven-de-espana-con-estrella-michelin/ |website=Restauración News |language=es |date=3 January 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> It stands at Calle Castillo 18, in the old town of Sagunto on the way up to the castle, in the former stables of the medieval palace of the Dukes of Gaeta, a space whose Gothic, Mozarabic and Romanesque stone arches were preserved in the dining room.<ref>{{cite web |title=Los nuevos restaurantes 1 Sol Guía Repsol 2021 |trans-title=The new 1 Sol Guía Repsol restaurants of 2021 |url=https://www.guiarepsol.com/es/soles-repsol/soles-2021/los-nuevos-restaurantes-1-sol-guia-repsol-2021/ |website=Guía Repsol |language=es |date=12 April 2021 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

Its name means "roots" in [[Valencian language]]. The offer is built around three menus, a weekday lunchtime option and the longer Saba and Arrels, the last two with vegetarian versions, and the raised upper part of the dining room holds an island where the chef finishes the first dessert in front of the guests.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arrels – Sagunt |url=https://guide.michelin.com/en/comunidad-valenciana/sagunt/restaurant/arrels |website=MICHELIN Guide |language=en |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The restaurant began by serving set menus at 15 euros and raised its prices only gradually, an approach Sevilla has defended as the sensible one for a small town, working with humble produce treated as carefully as if it were caviar; by 2022 its longest menu cost 92 euros.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pérez |first=Ana |title=Vicky Sevilla: "Comer un par de sándwiches en el aeropuerto es un robo, ir a Diverxo es un regalo" |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla: "Eating a couple of sandwiches at the airport is a rip-off, going to Diverxo is a gift" |url=https://www.esquire.com/es/donde-comer-beber/a41164654/vicky-sevilla-chef-estrella-michelin-diverxo/ |website=Esquire |language=es |date=30 September 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

=== Michelin star ===

Arrels first entered the Michelin Guide in the 2020 selection, in the Bib Gourmand category for good value, with the inspectors highlighting its technical cooking and the presentation of its dishes.<ref>{{cite web |last=Miñón |first=Matilde |title=La Comunidad Valenciana en la Guía MICHELIN 2020 |trans-title=The Valencian Community in the 2020 MICHELIN Guide |url=https://guide.michelin.com/es/es/articulo/dining-out/novedades-de-la-comunidad-valenciana-en-la-guia-michelin-2020 |website=MICHELIN Guide |language=es |date=17 February 2020 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

The gala presenting the ''MICHELIN Guide Spain & Portugal 2022'' was held on 14 December 2021 at the auditorium of the [[Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía]] in Valencia, the first time the city had hosted the ceremony.<ref>{{cite web |title=La Gala de presentación de la Guía MICHELIN España & Portugal 2022 tendrá lugar el 14 de diciembre en Valencia |trans-title=The presentation Gala of the MICHELIN Guide Spain & Portugal 2022 will take place on 14 December in Valencia |url=https://guide.michelin.com/es/es/articulo/news-and-views/la-gala-de-presentacion-de-la-guia-michelin-espana-portugal-2022-tendra-lugar-el-14-de-diciembre-en-valencia |website=MICHELIN Guide |language=es |date=1 June 2021 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> Arrels was among the restaurants awarded a first star at the ceremony; the mayor of Sagunto, Darío Moreno, described the award as "a milestone" in the history of the municipality.<ref>{{cite web |title=El destino turístico Sagunto entra en el universo Michelin gracias a la chef Vicky Sevilla y su restaurante Arrels |trans-title=The tourist destination Sagunto enters the Michelin universe thanks to chef Vicky Sevilla and her restaurant Arrels |url=https://aytosagunto.es/es/actualidad/restaurante-arrels-sagunto-estrella-michelin-enhorabuena-ayuntamiento-2021-12-15/ |website=Ayuntamiento de Sagunto |language=es |date=15 December 2021 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> Sevilla said afterwards that she had been overwhelmed and that the award reflected the work of the whole team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Arribas |first=Mónica |title=Vicky Sevilla: "Estoy como en una nube tras lograr la Estrella Michelín" |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla: "I am on a cloud after obtaining the Michelin Star" |url=https://www.levante-emv.com/morvedre/2021/12/15/vicky-sevilla-nube-lograr-estrella-60685568.html |website=Levante-EMV |language=es |date=15 December 2021 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The restaurant kept its star in the 2024 selection, announced in Barcelona in November 2023, when it was the only starred restaurant in the province of Valencia outside the provincial capital.<ref>{{cite web |title=El barrio de Valencia con más estrellas Michelín: cuatro restaurantes en solo 900 metros |trans-title=The neighbourhood of Valencia with the most Michelin stars: four restaurants in only 900 metres |url=https://www.elespanol.com/valencia/ocio/20231129/barrio-valencia-estrellas-michelin-solo900metros/813418878_0.html |website=El Español |language=es |date=29 November 2023 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==

In 2018, a year after opening Arrels, Sevilla was chosen Young Promise of the Valencian Community by the newspaper ''[[Levante-EMV]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=La chef Vicky Sevilla del restaurante Arrels de Sagunto queda finalista en el concurso Cocinero Revelación 2020 de Madrid Fusión |trans-title=Chef Vicky Sevilla of the Arrels restaurant in Sagunto is a finalist in the Cocinero Revelación 2020 competition at Madrid Fusión |url=https://aytosagunto.es/es/actualidad/la-chef-vicky-sevilla-del-restaurante-arrels-de-sagunto-queda-finalista-en-el-concurso-cocinero-revelacion-2020-de-madrid-fusion/ |website=Ayuntamiento de Sagunto |language=es |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In January 2020 she was one of eight candidates for the Cocinero Revelación prize at the [[Madrid Fusión]] congress, decided by a secret ballot of more than eighty gastronomic experts and won by Camila Ferraro of Sobretablas in Seville, the first woman to receive it.<ref>{{cite web |title=Camila Ferraro gana el premio Cocinero Revelación 2020 |trans-title=Camila Ferraro wins the Cocinero Revelación 2020 award |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/comer/al-dia/20200115/472911555882/camila-ferraro-premio-cocinero-revelacion-2020-madrid-fusion.html |website=La Vanguardia |language=es |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

In March 2023 she was named New Talent of the Year at the first edition of the La Liste Mediterranean special awards, presented in [[Monaco]] at a ceremony whose honorary prize went to [[Alain Ducasse]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Vicky Sevilla, premio New Talent of the Year de La Liste Mediterranean 2023 |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, New Talent of the Year award at La Liste Mediterranean 2023 |url=https://www.gastroeconomy.com/2023/03/vicky-sevilla-premio-new-talent-of-the-year-la-liste-mediterranean-2023/ |website=Gastroeconomy |language=es |date=24 March 2023 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In February 2024 she was chosen Chef of the Year 2023 by the Academy of Gastronomy of the Valencian Community, chaired by Belén Arias, at a gala attended by more than 500 guests.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vicky Sevilla, chef del año en Valencia |trans-title=Vicky Sevilla, chef of the year in Valencia |url=https://www.7canibales.com/noticias/vicky-sevilla-chef-del-ano-en-valencia/ |website=7 Caníbales |language=es |date=13 February 2024 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

In September 2022 the plenary of Sagunto town council approved the award of the city's Silver Medal to her, under her full name Victoria Sevilla Vázquez; the medals were presented on 9 October, the [[Day of the Valencian Community]].<ref>{{cite web |title=El Pleno Municipal acuerda la concesión de las Medallas de la Ciudad que se entregarán el próximo 9 de Octubre, Día de la Comunidad Valenciana |trans-title=The Municipal Plenary agrees the granting of the City Medals to be presented next 9 October, Day of the Valencian Community |url=https://aytosagunto.es/es/actualidad/el-pleno-municipal-acuerda-la-concesion-de-las-medallas-de-la-ciudad-que-se-entregaran-el-proximo-9-de-octubre-dia-de-la-comunidad-valenciana/ |website=Ayuntamiento de Sagunto |language=es |date=30 September 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In 2026 she received the Prix au Chef de l'Avenir of the Académie Internationale de la Gastronomie, an award for young cooks with a distinctive international projection; her candidacy was put forward by the Spanish Real Academia de Gastronomía, a founding member of the academy.<ref>{{cite web |title=La Real Academia de Gastronomía entrega los premios de la AIG 2026 |trans-title=The Royal Academy of Gastronomy presents the AIG 2026 awards |url=https://realacademiadegastronomia.com/entrega-premios-aig-2026-espanoles/ |website=Real Academia de Gastronomía |language=es |date=1 July 2026 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Lautaro Rigazzi Gaete''' (born 20 May 1998) is an Argentine-Chilean [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for Chilean club [[Rangers de Talca]].

==Career==
Born in [[Mendoza, Argentina]], Rigazzi was with local club Chacras before joining the [[Godoy Cruz Antonio Tomba|Godoy Cruz]] youth ranks. In 2019, he moved to Chile to play for [[Provincial Ovalle]]. The next years, he played for [[Comunal Cabrero]], [[Provincial Ranco]] and [[San Antonio Unido]].<ref name="olivares">{{cite web |last1=Olivares |first1=Brian |title=El defensor argentino que brilla en Segunda División y se inspira en figura de la U para llegar a La Roja |url=https://www.encancha.cl/entrevista/2022/10/14/el-defensor-argentino-que-brilla-en-segunda-division-se-inspira-en-figura-de-la-para-llegar-la-roja-183248/ |website=En Cancha |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es |date=14 October 2022}}</ref><ref name="ortega">{{cite web |last1=Ortega |first1=Pablo |title=“Si quiero llegar a Primera o salir de Chile, jugar un quinto año en Segunda me iba a estancar” |url=https://chile.as.com/futbol/si-quiero-llegar-a-primera-o-salir-de-chile-jugar-un-quinto-ano-en-segunda-me-iba-a-estancar-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es |date=10 February 2025}}</ref>

From 2022 to 2024, Rigazzi played for [[Deportes Concepción (Chile)|Deportes Concepción]],<ref name="olivares"/><ref name="ortega"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Campos |first1=Carlos |title=El caudillo Rigazzi encabeza las renovaciones en Deportes Concepción |url=https://www.diarioconcepcion.cl/deportes/2023/01/14/el-caudillo-rigazzi-encabeza-las-renovaciones-en-deportes-concepcion.html |website=Diario Concepción |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es |date=14 January 2023}}</ref> winning the [[2024 Segunda División Profesional de Chile]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lautaro Rigazzi y su reencuentro con Deportes Concepción |url=https://sabesdeportes.com/2025/04/24/lautaro-rigazzi-si-hubiese-sabido-que-deportes-concepcion-estaba-en-la-b-en-2025-renovaba-a-ojos-cerrados/ |website=sabesdeportes.com |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es |date=24 April 2025}}</ref> In 2025, he switched to [[Santiago Morning]], suffering a serious injury that kept him out of activity during the second half of the year.<ref name="sepulveda">{{cite news |last1=Sepúlveda |first1=Pablo |title=El ex Deportes Concepción Lautaro Rigazzi tiene nuevo club para la temporada 2026 |url=https://primerabchile.cl/lautaro-rigazzi-tiene-nuevo-club-para-la-temporada-2026/ |access-date=27 July 2026 |work=PrimeraBChile.cl |date=9 March 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="sifup">{{cite web |title=Lautaro Rigazzi y el Fondo de Lesiones Graves: “Es fundamental para apuntar a la mejor recuperación posible” |url=https://sifup.cl/web/2026/05/06/lautaro-rigazzi-y-el-fondo-de-lesiones-graves-es-fundamental-para-apuntar-a-la-mejor-recuperacion-posible/ |website=SIFUP |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es |date=6 May 2026}}</ref>

In March 2026, Rigazzi moved to Ecuador and joined [[Cumbayá F.C.|Cumbayá]].<ref name="sepulveda"/><ref name="sifup"/> He moved back to Chile and joined [[Rangers de Talca]] for the second half of the year.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Francke |first1=Lucas |title=No era Ramiro González: Rangers sorprende y suma a otro argentino nacionalizado chileno para la Primera B |url=https://www.encancha.cl/futbol-chileno/primera-b/2026/06/17/no-era-ramiro-gonzalez-rangers-sorprende-y-suma-a-otro-argentino-nacionalizado-chileno-para-la-primera-b/ |access-date=27 July 2026 |work=En Cancha |date=17 June 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=¿Serán titulares los cuatro refuerzos de Rangers en el partido ante Copiapó? |url=https://pasionporlosdeportes.cl/seran-titulares-los-cuatro-refuerzos-de-rangers-en-el-partido-ante-copiapo/ |website=Pasión Por Los Deportes |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es |date=25 July 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Rigazzi holds dual Argentine-Chilean nationality due to his mother's descent.<ref name="olivares"/>

'''Rebecca Lonedo''' (born 5 December 1996) is an Italian long-distance runner.<ref>{{cite web|website=World Athletics |title=Rebecca Lonedo|url=https://worldathletics.org/athletes/italy/rebecca-lonedo-14533436|accessdate=16 August 2026}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Arzignano]], she participated in dance and swimming before discovering athletics through cross-country races at school. She had a third place finish in her age-group at the 2013 Italian cross-country championship. In 2018, she won her first Italian title, with victory at the U23 level in the [[10,000 metres]] on the track. In 2021, she began to be coached by [[Stefano Baldini]], and that year made her [[half marathon]] debut. She was later coached by Massimo Magnani in [[Ferrara]] and is a member of [[Fiamme Oro]].<ref>{{cite web|website=Fidal |title=Rebecca Lonedo|url= https://www.fidal.it/atleta/LONEDO-Rebecca/eK6RkpihbGw= |accessdate=16 August 2026}}</ref><ref> {{cite web|date=31 January 2026|url=https://www.lapressa.it/articoli/sport/alla-corrida-dei-record-vincono-pietro-riva-e-rebecca-lonedo#google_vignette|website=Lapressa|title= Pietro Riva and Rebecca Lonedo win the record-breaking bullfight |accessdate=16 August 2026}}</ref>

Lonedo placed seventh in the individual marathon and won the silver medal in the team event with Italy at the [[2025 European Running Championships]] in Belgium.<ref>{{Cite web | url= https://www.european-athletics.com/home/news/belgium-1-2-herbiet-and-thomas-make-half-marathon-history-at-european-running-championships 
|title= Belgium 1-2! Herbiet and Thomas make half marathon history at European Running Championships|first=
Chris |last=Broadbent|date=
12 Apr 2025
|access-date=16 August 2026| website=European Athletics}}</ref> She placed twentieth overall at the [[2025 World Athletics Championships – Women's marathon| 2025 World Athletics Championships]] in Tokyo, running 2:33:40 for the marathon, only her second race at the distance.<ref>{{Cite web | url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7190593?eventId=10229534
|title= World Athletics Championships, Tokyo 2025 
|access-date=16 August 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|website=OA Sport|url= https://www.oasport.it/2025/10/rebecca-lonedo-la-nuova-maratoneta-azzurra-lemozione-dei-miei-primi-mondiali-sprint-zone/ |title=Rebecca Lonedo, the new Italian marathon runner: "The emotion of my first World Championships"|accessdate=16 August 2026}}</ref> She improved her marathon times steadily with 2:28:42 at the [[Hamburg Marathon]] and 2:24:28 at the [[Seville Marathon]] in February 2026, just 75 seconds off the Italian record.<ref>{{cite web|title=Interview with Rebecca Lonedo: "Running is something I feel inside, it's always been a part of me, and that makes everything easier."|first= Dario|last= Marchini |accessdate=16 August 2026|date=18 Feb 2026|url= https://www.therunningclub.it/2026/02/18/intervista-rebecca-lonedo-post-maratona-siviglia-andrea-soffientini-pacer/ |website=The Running Club}}</ref> On 16 August, she placed sixth in the individual race and won the silver medal with Italy in the women’s team  marathon at the [[2026 European Athletics Championships]] in Birmingham, England.<ref>{{cite web|title= Rebecca Lonedo sixth in the Birmingham Marathon and silver in the team event|date= August 16, 2026|accessdate=August 16, 2026|url= https://www.ilgiornaledivicenza.it/argomenti/sport/altri-sport/rebecca-lonedo-sesta-nella-maratona-di-birmingham-e-argento-a-squadre-1.13098538/amp
|website= ilgiornaledivicenza.it}}</ref>
